```html
          <section class="article-section" id="setup">
            <h2>Setup and updates</h2>
            <div class="faq-list">
              <details class="faq-item" id="install">
                <summary>How do I install REA?</summary>
                <p>
                  With Node.js and npm available, run setup, choose your coding
                  agent and review the proposed changes.
                </p>
                <div class="code-block">
                  <div class="code-header">
                    <span>Terminal · agent setup</span
                    ><button
                      class="copy-button"
                      type="button"
                      data-copy="faq-setup"
                      aria-label="Copy REA setup command"
                    >
                      Copy
                    </button>
                  </div>
                  <pre><code id="faq-setup">npx rea-agents@latest setup</code></pre>
                </div>
                <p>
                  Setup registers REA's MCP connection and installs the matching
                  investigation skill. Restart your agent when it finishes, then
                  give it a target path and a question.
                  <a href="../get-started/">Follow the setup guide</a> for
                  prerequisites and your first analysis.
                </p>
              </details>
              <details class="faq-item" id="agents">
                <summary>Which coding agents can use REA?</summary>
                <p>
                  Any agent that supports local MCP servers. Setup includes
                  Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI,
                  Windsurf, Devin, OpenCode, Antigravity, GitHub Copilot CLI,
                  Command Code, Grok Build, and VS Code. Grok Bot's connector is
                  added from its chat.
                </p>
                <p>
                  <a href="../get-started/#agent">Connect your coding agent</a>.
                </p>
              </details>
              <details class="faq-item" id="update">
                <summary>How do I update REA?</summary>
                <p>
                  REA releases frequently, including bug fixes. If you installed
                  the CLI with npm:
                </p>
                <div class="code-block">
                  <div class="code-header">
                    <span>Terminal · installed CLI</span
                    ><button
                      class="copy-button"
                      type="button"
                      data-copy="faq-update-cli"
                      aria-label="Copy REA update command"
                    >
                      Copy
                    </button>
                  </div>
                  <pre><code id="faq-update-cli">rea update</code></pre>
                </div>
                <p>
                  Follow the setup refresh command printed by the update. If you
                  set up your agent through <code>npx</code>, run:
                </p>
                <div class="code-block">
                  <div class="code-header">
                    <span>Terminal · refresh agent setup</span
                    ><button
                      class="copy-button"
                      type="button"
                      data-copy="faq-update-agent"
                      aria-label="Copy agent setup refresh command"
                    >
                      Copy
                    </button>
                  </div>
                  <pre><code id="faq-update-agent">npx rea-agents@latest setup</code></pre>
                </div>
                <p>
                  Review the changes and restart your agent. Its REA connection
                  pins a package version, so refreshing setup makes it use the
                  new release. For one-off CLI commands, use
                  <code>npx -y rea-agents@latest</code> followed by the command.
                </p>
              </details>
              <details class="faq-item" id="skill">
                <summary>
                  Is installing the skill from skills.sh enough?
                </summary>
                <p>
                  The skill gives your agent investigation instructions. Run
                  <a href="#install">REA setup</a> to connect the MCP server and
                  install the matching skill, then restart your agent so it can
                  call the tools.
                </p>
              </details>
            </div>
          </section>

          <section class="article-section" id="analysis">
            <h2>Analysis</h2>
            <div class="faq-list">
              <details class="faq-item" id="targets">
                <summary>What can I analyze with REA?</summary>
                <p>Start with the kind of software you have:</p>
                <ul>
                  <li>
                    <a href="../guides/native/"
                      >Native executables and libraries</a
                    >: functions, assembly, pseudocode and references.
                  </li>
                  <li>
                    <a href="../guides/javascript/"
                      >JavaScript and Electron apps</a
                    >: modules, imports, IPC and source locations.
                  </li>
                  <li>
                    <a href="../guides/browser/">Browser pages</a>: scripts,
                    requests and runtime observations.
                  </li>
                </ul>
                <p>
                  REA also has workflows for managed assemblies, Android APKs,
                  firmware and packaged resources.
                  <a href="../showcase/">See the case studies</a> for worked
                  investigations.
                </p>
              </details>
              <details class="faq-item" id="providers">
                <summary>Do I need Hopper, Ghidra or IDA?</summary>
                <p>
                  Deep native analysis uses one of them. Static JavaScript and
                  .NET inspection work with the supplied files and do not need a
                  native analysis engine.
                </p>
                <p>
                  Connect your existing Ghidra or IDA installation, or let setup
                  detect Hopper and propose an installation. Your host and
                  target determine which provider can be used.
                  <a href="../get-started/#native">Set up native analysis</a>.
                </p>
              </details>
              <details class="faq-item" id="cli">
                <summary>Can I use REA without a coding agent?</summary>
                <p>
                  Yes. The CLI uses the same analysis workflows. For a local
                  JavaScript or Electron app:
                </p>
                <div class="code-block">
                  <div class="code-header">
                    <span>Terminal · static application analysis</span
                    ><button
                      class="copy-button"
                      type="button"
                      data-copy="faq-cli-analysis"
                      aria-label="Copy REA CLI analysis command"
                    >
                      Copy
                    </button>
                  </div>
                  <pre><code id="faq-cli-analysis">npx -y rea-agents@latest analyze-javascript-application \
  /absolute/path/to/app --json</code></pre>
                </div>
                <p>
                  Replace the path with an extracted application folder or ASAR
                  file. <a href="../get-started/#terminal">Use the CLI</a> for
                  installation options.
                </p>
              </details>
              <details class="faq-item" id="code">
                <summary>What code does REA return?</summary>
                <p>
                  Native analysis returns assembly and pseudocode, with calls,
                  references and relevant constants. JavaScript analysis returns
                  modules, their relationships and source locations.
                </p>
                <p>
                  Your agent uses these findings to explain the behavior or
                  write and test an implementation. The
                  <a href="../showcase/dx-ball/#sound-pan"
                    >DX-Ball calculation</a
                  >
                  and <a href="../showcase/ctf/">CTF flag checker</a> show how
                  that process works.
                </p>
              </details>
              <details class="faq-item" id="prompt">
                <summary>What should I ask my agent?</summary>
                <p>
                  Give it a local target and one behavior to investigate. For a
                  JavaScript or Electron app:
                </p>
                <div class="agent-terminal">
                  <div class="terminal-header">
                    <span class="terminal-title"
                      ><span class="terminal-dots" aria-hidden="true"
                        ><i></i><i></i><i></i></span
                      >Your coding agent</span
                    ><button
                      class="copy-button"
                      type="button"
                      data-copy="faq-analysis-prompt"
                      aria-label="Copy example analysis prompt"
                    >
                      Copy
                    </button>
                  </div>
                  <p class="terminal-prompt">
                    <span class="prompt-symbol" aria-hidden="true">›</span
                    ><span id="faq-analysis-prompt"
                      >Use REA to analyze /absolute/path/to/app and explain how
                      it exports data. Show the relevant code and source
                      locations.</span
                    ><span class="terminal-cursor" aria-hidden="true"></span>
                  </p>
                </div>
                <p class="caption">
                  Replace the path with your target. The
                  <a href="../guides/">guides</a> provide prompts for native,
                  Electron and browser examples.
                </p>
              </details>
            </div>
          </section>

          <section class="article-section" id="troubleshooting">
            <h2>Troubleshooting</h2>
            <div class="faq-list">
              <details class="faq-item" id="connection">
                <summary>Why can't my agent see the REA tools?</summary>
                <p>
                  Restart or reconnect your agent after setup. Check its REA
                  registration with <code>doctor</code>; for Codex:
                </p>
                <div class="code-block">
                  <div class="code-header">
                    <span>Terminal · check one client</span
                    ><button
                      class="copy-button"
                      type="button"
                      data-copy="faq-doctor"
                      aria-label="Copy client diagnosis command"
                    >
                      Copy
                    </button>
                  </div>
                  <pre><code id="faq-doctor">npx -y rea-agents@latest doctor --client codex --json</code></pre>
                </div>
                <p>
                  Replace <code>codex</code> with your client ID, such as
                  <code>claude_code</code> or <code>cursor</code>. If the report
                  shows a missing or stale registration, run setup for that
                  client:
                </p>
                <div class="code-block">
                  <div class="code-header">
                    <span>Terminal · repair one client's setup</span
                    ><button
                      class="copy-button"
                      type="button"
                      data-copy="faq-repair"
                      aria-label="Copy scoped setup command"
                    >
                      Copy
                    </button>
                  </div>
                  <pre><code id="faq-repair">npx rea-agents@latest setup --client codex</code></pre>
                </div>
                <p>
                  Review its plan and restart the client. If registration is
                  healthy but tools remain absent, check the client's MCP
                  connection error.
                  <a href="../get-started/#help">More setup diagnostics</a>.
                </p>
              </details>
              <details class="faq-item" id="hopper">
                <summary>Do I need to start Hopper first?</summary>
                <p>
                  REA starts Hopper when an operation needs it. On macOS,
                  complete the first-run choice of demo mode or license
                  activation before unattended analysis.
                  <a href="../get-started/#native">See native provider setup</a
                  >.
                </p>
              </details>
              <details class="faq-item" id="bugs">
                <summary>What should I do if I hit a bug?</summary>
                <p>
                  <a href="#update">Update REA</a>, restart your agent and retry
                  the same task. A recent release may already fix the problem.
                </p>
                <p>
                  If it persists,
                  <a href="https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/new/choose"
                    >open an issue</a
                  >
                  with your REA version, operating system, target type, steps to
                  reproduce and error output. Include the provider name when the
                  problem involves native analysis.
                </p>
              </details>
            </div>
          </section>

          <section class="article-section" id="sharing">
            <h2>Data and sharing</h2>
            <div class="faq-list">
              <details class="faq-item" id="privacy">
                <summary>Does REA upload my app?</summary>
                <p>
                  REA analyzes targets on your machine. Your agent receives the
                  results, and its model provider's data policy applies to those
                  results.
                </p>
              </details>
              <details class="faq-item" id="contribute">
                <summary>How can I share an example or contribute?</summary>
                <p>
                  Have a useful REA example? We'd love to see it. Share the
                  target, your question, the findings and how you checked them
                  in an
                  <a href="https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/new/choose"
                    >issue</a
                  >
                  or
                  <a href="https://github.com/morluto/rea/pulls">pull request</a
                  >. Short code excerpts and figures help others follow the
                  investigation.
                </p>
                <p>
                  Bug reports, feature requests, documentation and code
                  improvements are welcome too. You can also discuss an example
                  in the <a href="https://discord.gg/GkcryMnJDM">community</a>.
                </p>
              </details>
            </div>
          </section>
        </article>
      </div>
    </main>
    <footer class="site-footer">
      <div class="container footer-inner">
        <p>REA · Reverse Engineer Anything</p>
        <div class="footer-links">

</html>
```

```html
          <section class="article-section" id="setup">
            <h2>1. Connect your agent to REA</h2>
            <p>
              Use a coding agent such as Claude Code, Codex or Cursor. You’ll
              need Node.js and npm; the
              <a href="../get-started/">setup guide lists supported versions</a
              >.
            </p>

                  Copy

                <span class="prompt-symbol" aria-hidden="true">›</span

                  >Install REA and connect it to this coding agent using npx
                  rea-agents@latest setup. Show me the setup plan for approval,
                  then verify the installation.</span
                ><span class="terminal-cursor" aria-hidden="true"></span>
              </p>
            </div>
            <p class="caption">Or run this command in your terminal:</p>
            <div class="code-block code-inline">
              <code id="first-setup-command">npx rea-agents@latest setup</code>
              <button
                class="copy-button"
                type="button"
                data-copy="first-setup-command"
                aria-label="Copy setup command"
              >
                Copy
              </button>
            </div>
            <p>
              Review the plan, approve the setup, then restart your agent.
              Already connected? Continue below.
            </p>
          </section>
          <section class="article-section" id="ask">
            <h2>2. Ask where the CSV is written</h2>
            <p>
              The example is a six-file Electron app with an
              <strong>Export notes</strong> button. Your agent can inspect its
              code without installing or launching Electron.
            </p>
            <div class="agent-terminal">
              <div class="terminal-header">
                <span class="terminal-title"
                  ><span class="terminal-dots" aria-hidden="true"
                    ><i></i><i></i><i></i></span
                  >Your coding agent</span
                >
                <button
                  class="copy-button"
                  type="button"
                  data-copy="first-analysis-prompt"
                  aria-label="Copy Notes investigation prompt"
                >
                  Copy
                </button>
              </div>
              <p class="terminal-prompt">
                <span class="prompt-symbol" aria-hidden="true">›</span
                ><span id="first-analysis-prompt"
                  >Download https://rea.tools/examples/notes-example.zip into a
                  new example folder and unpack it. Use REA to find what happens
                  when I click Export notes. Show where notes.csv is written,
                  which fields it contains, and the relevant files and
                  lines.</span
                ><span class="terminal-cursor" aria-hidden="true"></span>
              </p>
            </div>
            <p>
              Your agent downloads the files and gives the unpacked folder to
              REA for inspection.
            </p>
            <p>
              <a
                class="button"
                href="../examples/notes-example.zip"
                download="notes-example.zip"
                >Download example ZIP</a
              >
            </p>
            <p class="caption">
              If your agent can’t download files, unzip this archive yourself.
              Give it the path to the <code>notes-example</code> folder and the
              same export question.
            </p>
          </section>
          <section class="article-section" id="answer">
            <h2>3. Follow the answer back to the code</h2>
            <p>Look for a short explanation with file and line references:</p>
            <blockquote class="prompt">
              <p>
                The button sends a <code>notes:export</code> message. The main
                process formats the notes as CSV and writes
                <code>notes.csv</code> in the user’s Downloads folder. The
                columns are <code>id</code> and <code>title</code>.
              </p>
            </blockquote>
            <figure class="workflow-figure">
              <p class="figure-title">From the button to the file writer</p>
              <ol class="flow-steps">
                <li>
                  <span class="flow-label">Page · renderer.js</span
                  ><span class="flow-node">Export notes</span
                  ><span class="flow-note"
                    >Calls <code>notes.exportCsv()</code>.</span
                  >
                </li>
                <li>
                  <span class="flow-label">Bridge · preload.js</span
                  ><span class="flow-node"><code>notes:export</code></span
                  ><span class="flow-note"
                    >Sends a named message to the main process.</span
                  >
                </li>
                <li>
                  <span class="flow-label">Handler · main.js</span
                  ><span class="flow-node">Write notes.csv</span
                  ><span class="flow-note"
                    >Calls the formatter in <code>csv.js</code> and writes the
                    file.</span
                  >
                </li>
              </ol>
              <figcaption>
                REA’s static analysis pairs the message with its handler. The
                destination is read from code.
              </figcaption>
            </figure>
            <div class="code-block">
              <div class="code-header">
                <span>main.js · lines 8–12</span
                ><a href="../examples/notes-electron/main.js">Source</a>
              </div>
              <pre><code>ipcMain.handle("notes:export", () =&gt; {
  const destination = path.join(app.getPath("downloads"), "notes.csv");
  writeFileSync(destination, toCsv(notes), "utf8");
  return destination;
});</code></pre>
            </div>
            <p>
              The file path, formatter and write call are together in this
              handler. Ask your agent to show these lines if its answer leaves
              them out.
            </p>
            <p>
              <a href="../guides/javascript/#follow"
                >See the full code trace and recorded REA result</a
              >.
            </p>
          </section>
          <section class="article-section" id="check">
            <h2>4. Check a prediction</h2>
            <p>
              A comma separates CSV columns. What happens when a note title
              itself contains a comma or quotation marks?
            </p>
            <div class="agent-terminal">
              <div class="terminal-header">
                <span class="terminal-title"
                  ><span class="terminal-dots" aria-hidden="true"
                    ><i></i><i></i><i></i></span
                  >Your coding agent</span
                >
                <button
                  class="copy-button"
                  type="button"
                  data-copy="first-check-prompt"
                  aria-label="Copy CSV check prompt"
                >
                  Copy
                </button>
              </div>
              <p class="terminal-prompt">
                <span class="prompt-symbol" aria-hidden="true">›</span
                ><span id="first-check-prompt"
                  >Predict the CSV for a note with id 1 and title Hello, "REA".
                  Then run the example’s toCsv formatter with Node.js to check
                  it. Show the prediction and actual output.</span
                ><span class="terminal-cursor" aria-hidden="true"></span>
              </p>
            </div>
            <div class="code-block">
              <div class="code-header">
                <span>Expected formatter output</span>
              </div>
              <pre><code>id,title
1,"Hello, ""REA"""</code></pre>
            </div>
            <p>
              The title stays in one quoted field; each quotation mark is
              doubled. This checks the formatter directly with Node.js.
            </p>
            <details class="evidence-details">
              <summary>Run the check yourself</summary>
              <p>
                Open a terminal in the unpacked
                <code>notes-example</code> folder:
              </p>
              <div class="code-block">
                <div class="code-header">
                  <span>Node.js · CSV formatter</span
                  ><button
                    class="copy-button"
                    type="button"
                    data-copy="first-check-command"
                    aria-label="Copy formatter check command"
                  >
                    Copy
                  </button>
                </div>
                <pre><code id="first-check-command">node &lt;&lt;'JS'
const { toCsv } = require('./csv.js');
process.stdout.write(toCsv([{ id: 1, title: 'Hello, "REA"' }]));
JS</code></pre>
              </div>
              <p class="caption">
                This command uses a shell with here-document support, such as
                Bash or Zsh. Your agent can run the same JavaScript in your
                platform’s shell.
              </p>
            </details>
          </section>
          <section class="article-section" id="next">
```

```html
    <main id="main" class="container">
      <div class="page-heading">
        <p class="breadcrumb"><a href="../">Home</a> / Get started</p>
        <h1>Set up REA.</h1>
        <p class="lede">
          Connect REA to your coding agent, or inspect a local app from your
          terminal.
        </p>
        <p class="requirements">
          You'll need Node.js 22 (22.19+), 24 (24.11+) or 26+, and npm.
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="article-layout">
        <nav class="contents" aria-label="On this page">
          <p>Setup options</p>
          <ul>
            <li><a href="#agent">Connect your coding agent</a></li>
            <li><a href="#terminal">Use the CLI</a></li>
            <li><a href="#native">Set up native analysis</a></li>
            <li><a href="#help">Getting help</a></li>
          </ul>
        </nav>
        <article class="article" aria-label="REA getting started guide">
          <section class="article-section" id="agent">
            <h2>Connect your coding agent</h2>
            <p>
              Run setup to connect REA to your coding agent. Client choices
              include Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Windsurf, Grok
              Build, and other supported MCP clients. Grok Bot's connector is
              added from its chat.
            </p>
            <div class="agent-terminal">
              <div class="terminal-header">
                <span class="terminal-title"
                  ><span class="terminal-dots" aria-hidden="true"
                    ><i></i><i></i><i></i></span
                  >Your coding agent</span
                >
                <button
                  class="copy-button"
                  type="button"
                  data-copy="agent-install-prompt"
                  aria-label="Copy REA installation prompt"
                >
                  Copy
                </button>
              </div>
              <p class="terminal-prompt">
                <span class="prompt-symbol" aria-hidden="true">›</span
                ><span id="agent-install-prompt"
                  >Install REA and connect it to this coding agent using npx
                  rea-agents@latest setup. Show me the setup plan for approval,
                  then verify the installation.</span
                ><span class="terminal-cursor" aria-hidden="true"></span>
              </p>
            </div>
            <details class="evidence-details">
              <summary>Or run setup yourself</summary>
              <div class="code-block">
                <div class="code-header">
                  <span>Terminal</span
                  ><button
                    class="copy-button"
                    type="button"
                    data-copy="agent-setup"
                    aria-label="Copy agent setup command"
                  >
                    Copy
                  </button>
                </div>
                <pre><code id="agent-setup">npx rea-agents@latest setup</code></pre>
              </div>
            </details>
            <p>
              Choose your client and review the setup plan. REA adds its MCP
              connection and the matching investigation skill, keeping a backup
              of existing configuration. It asks before applying the changes.
            </p>
            <p>
              Restart your client when setup finishes. Give your agent a target
              path and a specific question. For a JavaScript or Electron app,
              you might start with:
            </p>
            <blockquote class="prompt">
              <p>
                Look at <code>/absolute/path/to/app</code> and find how it
                exports data. Show the entry points, calls and dependencies
                involved, with the source locations for your findings.
              </p>
            </blockquote>
            <p>Replace the path with your local target.</p>
          </section>

          <section class="article-section" id="terminal">
            <h2>Use the CLI</h2>
            <p>
              Analyze a JavaScript or Electron application folder or ASAR
              archive without running the app:
            </p>
            <div class="code-block">
              <div class="code-header">
                <span>Static application analysis</span
                ><button
                  class="copy-button"
                  type="button"
                  data-copy="terminal-analysis"
                  aria-label="Copy JavaScript analysis command"
                >
                  Copy
                </button>
              </div>
              <pre><code id="terminal-analysis">npx -y rea-agents@latest analyze-javascript-application \
  /absolute/path/to/app --json</code></pre>
            </div>
            <p>
              Replace the path with your extracted app directory or
              <code>.asar</code> file. On Windows, a path such as
              <code>"D:/apps/example"</code> works here.
            </p>
            <p>
              The result identifies the app, shows connections between modules
              and gives their source locations. Connections REA cannot resolve
              are marked in the result.
            </p>
            <p>
              If you'd like a permanent <code>rea</code> command in your shell:
            </p>
            <div class="code-block">
              <div class="code-header">
                <span>Install the CLI</span
                ><button
                  class="copy-button"
                  type="button"
                  data-copy="install-cli"
                  aria-label="Copy CLI installation command"
                >
                  Copy
                </button>
              </div>
              <pre><code id="install-cli">npm install --global rea-agents</code></pre>
            </div>
            <p>
              <a href="../guides/javascript/"
                >Continue with the JavaScript application guide</a
              >
            </p>
          </section>

          <section class="article-section" id="native">
            <h2>Set up native analysis</h2>
            <p>
              Native binaries need a local analysis tool. Choose and configure
              one below, then give REA your executable or library.
            </p>
            <details class="evidence-details">
              <summary>Choose a tool: Ghidra, Hopper or IDA</summary>
              <div class="provider-list">
                <div class="provider">
                  <h3>Ghidra</h3>
                  <div>
                    <p>
                      Use an existing Ghidra 12.1.x installation and a 64-bit
                      JDK 21 or newer on Linux x64 or macOS x64/arm64. Set the
                      paths before running setup:
                    </p>
                    <details class="evidence-details">
                      <summary>Connect your Ghidra installation</summary>
                      <div class="code-block">
                        <div class="code-header">
                          <span>Ghidra connection · macOS / Linux</span
                          ><button
                            class="copy-button"
                            type="button"
                            data-copy="ghidra-connect"
                            aria-label="Copy ghidra connection · macos / linux"
                          >
                            Copy
                          </button>
                        </div>
                        <pre><code id="ghidra-connect">export GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR=/absolute/path/to/ghidra_12.1.4_PUBLIC
export JAVA_HOME=/absolute/path/to/jdk-21
npx -y rea-agents@latest doctor --provider ghidra --json
npx rea-agents@latest setup</code></pre>
                      </div>
                      <p>
                        Replace both paths with your existing installations.
                        Setup checks them and records valid settings for your
                        selected client. On macOS, use a Ghidra package with the
                        native decompiler matching your host architecture.
                      </p>
                    </details>
                  </div>
                </div>
                <div class="provider">
                  <h3>Hopper</h3>
                  <div>
                    <p>
                      Connect Hopper on macOS or Linux. Run the setup command
                      above; it detects an existing installation or offers an
                      installation plan for your approval.
                    </p>
                    <p>
                      On macOS, complete Hopper's first-run choice of demo mode
                      or license activation before an unattended analysis.
                    </p>
                  </div>
                </div>
                <div class="provider">
                  <h3>IDA</h3>
                  <div>
                    <p>
                      The verified IDA setups use Windows, with an existing MCP
                      registration for an attached GUI or a headless database.
                      Linux and macOS headless analysis remains unverified.
                    </p>
                    <details class="evidence-details">
                      <summary>
                        Connect an existing IDA MCP registration
                      </summary>
                      <p>
                        Keep the upstream server's working <code>command</code>,
                        <code>args</code> and optional <code>env</code> in a
                        JSON file. An existing <code>mcpServers</code> object
                        with an <code>ida-pro-mcp</code> entry is also accepted.
                        Point REA at that file before setup:
                      </p>
                      <div class="code-block">
                        <div class="code-header">
                          <span>IDA connection · Windows PowerShell</span
                          ><button
                            class="copy-button"
                            type="button"
                            data-copy="ida-connect"
                            aria-label="Copy IDA connection for Windows PowerShell"
                          >
                            Copy
                          </button>
                        </div>
                        <pre><code id="ida-connect">$env:REA_IDA_MCP_CONFIG = "C:/analysis/ida-mcp.json"
$env:REA_ANALYSIS_PROVIDER = "ida"
npx -y rea-agents@latest doctor --provider ida --json
npx rea-agents@latest setup</code></pre>
                      </div>
                      <p>
                        The attached profile uses upstream legacy 1.4.0 tools
                        with the original binary already open in IDA. The
                        headless profile uses the upstream database-supervisor
                        API and a registration with
                        <code>"mode": "headless"</code>; real verification
                        covers an IDA 9.3 Windows x64 supervisor. Doctor checks
                        the registration without starting IDA.
                      </p>
                      <p>
                        Give REA the original executable path, with
                        <code>--provider ida</code> in a CLI query. For an
                        agent, include <code>REA_IDA_MCP_CONFIG</code> in the
                        REA registration's environment and select IDA when
                        opening the binary.
                      </p>
                    </details>
                  </div>
                </div>
              </div>
            </details>
            <p class="small-heading">
              For an existing Ghidra setup, inspect a function with:
            </p>
            <div class="code-block">
              <div class="code-header">
                <span>Function analysis</span
                ><button
                  class="copy-button"
                  type="button"
                  data-copy="native-function"
                  aria-label="Copy native function analysis command"
                >
                  Copy
                </button>
              </div>
              <pre><code id="native-function">npx -y rea-agents@latest function /absolute/path/to/program main \
  --provider ghidra --json</code></pre>
            </div>
            <p>
              Replace <code>main</code> with the function name or address you
              want to inspect.
            </p>
            <details class="evidence-details">
              <summary>How native analysis sessions work</summary>
              <p>
                Each CLI command imports and analyzes the binary, then closes
                its session. Your agent's MCP queries reuse the imported binary
                while that session is open.
              </p>
            </details>
            <p>
              <a href="../guides/native/">Follow a native analysis example</a>
              to see how the function result leads to a recovered calculation.
            </p>
          </section>

          <section class="article-section" id="help">
            <h2>Getting help</h2>
            <h3>If your agent doesn't see REA</h3>
            <p>
              Restart or reconnect the client after setup. Check its REA
              connection with <code>doctor</code>; for Codex:
            </p>
            <div class="code-block">
              <div class="code-header">
                <span>Check one client</span
                ><button
                  class="copy-button"
                  type="button"
                  data-copy="client-doctor"
                  aria-label="Copy client diagnosis command"
                >
                  Copy
                </button>
              </div>
              <pre><code id="client-doctor">npx -y rea-agents@latest doctor --client codex --json</code></pre>
            </div>
            <h3 class="small-heading">If a provider needs attention</h3>
            <p>Check the provider you're using. For Ghidra:</p>
            <div class="code-block">
              <div class="code-header">
                <span>Check one provider</span
                ><button
                  class="copy-button"
                  type="button"
                  data-copy="provider-doctor"
                  aria-label="Copy provider diagnosis command"
                >
                  Copy
                </button>
              </div>
              <pre><code id="provider-doctor">npx -y rea-agents@latest doctor --provider ghidra --json</code></pre>
            </div>
            <p>The report gives the failed check and a suggested next step.</p>

          </section>
```

```html
        </p>
        <h1>See what happens<br />when you click.</h1>
        <p class="lede">
          Use a small browser app to connect an action, its network request and
          the JavaScript that builds a download.
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="article-layout">
        <nav class="contents" aria-label="On this page">
          <p>In this guide</p>

        <article class="article" aria-label="Browser observation">
          <section class="article-section" id="example">
            <h2>What happens when you click Export?</h2>
            <p>
              The
              <a href="../../examples/notes-web/">Notes browser example</a> has
              an <strong>Export notes</strong> button. Clicking it loads
              <code>notes.json</code>, formats the two notes as CSV, and starts
              a download.
            </p>
            <figure class="workflow-figure">
              <p class="figure-title">From the click to the CSV download</p>
              <ol class="flow-steps">
                <li>
                  <span class="flow-label">01 · You</span
                  ><span class="flow-node">Click Export notes</span
                  ><span class="flow-note"
                    >Perform the action in your browser while the capture is
                    running.</span
                  >
                </li>
                <li>
                  <span class="flow-label">02 · REA</span
                  ><span class="flow-node">Record the request</span
                  ><span class="flow-note"
                    >Capture the request URL, response status and JSON structure
                    from the selected page.</span
                  >
                </li>
                <li>
                  <span class="flow-label">03 · Your agent</span
                  ><span class="flow-node">Read the export code</span
                  ><span class="flow-note"
                    >Connect the observed request to
                    <code>fetch("./notes.json")</code> in
                    <code>export.js</code>.</span
                  >
                </li>
              </ol>
              <p class="flow-result">
                <code>GET notes.json → 200 → notes[] → CSV</code>
              </p>
              <figcaption>
                Start the capture before clicking Export notes.
              </figcaption>
            </figure>
          </section>
          <section class="article-section" id="prepare">
            <h2>Open Chrome with remote debugging</h2>
            <p>
              Open the hosted Notes example with a separate browser profile and
              a local debugging port. On Linux:
            </p>
            <div class="code-block">
              <div class="code-header">
                <span>Start the example browser</span
                ><button
                  class="copy-button"
                  type="button"
                  data-copy="browser-start"
                  aria-label="Copy start the example browser"
                >
                  Copy
                </button>
              </div>
              <pre><code id="browser-start">google-chrome \
  --remote-debugging-port=9222 \
  --user-data-dir=/tmp/rea-notes-browser \
  https://rea.tools/examples/notes-web/</code></pre>
            </div>
            <p>
              Use your installed browser's executable path on macOS or Windows.
              You can replace the page URL with another page you want to
              inspect.
            </p>
            <p>
              REA connects to this existing browser. You keep control of the
              page, perform the action, and close the browser when finished.
            </p>
          </section>
          <section class="article-section" id="ask">
            <h2>Ask your agent to watch one action</h2>
            <div class="agent-terminal">
              <div class="terminal-header">
                <span class="terminal-title"
                  ><span class="terminal-dots" aria-hidden="true"
                    ><i></i><i></i><i></i></span
                  >Your coding agent</span
                ><button
                  class="copy-button"
                  type="button"
                  data-copy="browser-prompt"
                  aria-label="Copy example prompt"
                >
                  Copy
                </button>
              </div>
              <p class="terminal-prompt">
                <span class="prompt-symbol" aria-hidden="true">›</span
                ><span id="browser-prompt"
                  >Use REA to inspect this page while I click Export notes. What
                  request does it make, and how is the CSV built?</span
                ><span class="terminal-cursor" aria-hidden="true"></span>
              </p>
            </div>
            <p class="caption">
              Example prompt. Give your agent the debugging endpoint,
              <code>http://127.0.0.1:9222</code>, and the page URL. Let it start
              the capture before you click.
            </p>
            <p>
              Your agent discovers the page target, starts an observation
              window, and reads the resulting evidence. It can then inspect the
              script behind the export.
            </p>
          </section>
          <section class="article-section" id="capture">
            <h2>Or capture from the terminal</h2>
            <p>Find the page's target ID:</p>
            <div class="code-block">
              <div class="code-header">
                <span>Find the page</span
                ><button
                  class="copy-button"
                  type="button"
                  data-copy="browser-targets"
                  aria-label="Copy find the page"
                >
                  Copy
                </button>
              </div>
              <pre><code id="browser-targets">npx -y rea-agents@latest list-browser-targets \
  http://127.0.0.1:9222 --json</code></pre>
            </div>
            <p>
              Choose the target with the Notes example URL. Replace
              <code>TARGET_ID</code> below with its ID, then run:
            </p>
            <div class="code-block">
              <div class="code-header">
                <span>Capture the next ten seconds</span
                ><button
                  class="copy-button"
                  type="button"
                  data-copy="browser-capture"
                  aria-label="Copy capture the next ten seconds"
                >
                  Copy
                </button>
              </div>
              <pre><code id="browser-capture">npx -y rea-agents@latest inspect-web-page \
  http://127.0.0.1:9222 TARGET_ID \
  --observation-ms 10000 \
  --include-accessibility-text \
  --include-json-body-shapes --json</code></pre>
            </div>
            <p>
              Let the command connect for a few seconds, then click
              <strong>Export notes</strong> in that browser. The result arrives
              after the observation window ends.
            </p>
            <p>
              The captured result includes the selected page, network activity
              during that window, and the shape of the JSON response. Earlier
              requests are outside this capture.
            </p>
          </section>
          <section class="article-section" id="result">
            <h2>Read the request and export script</h2>
            <div class="evidence-table-wrap">
              <table class="evidence-table">
                <caption>
                  Recorded with REA 4.1.0 on the local Notes example
                </caption>
                <thead>
                  <tr>
                    <th>Captured fact</th>
                    <th>Value</th>
                  </tr>
                </thead>
                <tbody>
                  <tr>
                    <td>Request</td>
                    <td><code>GET /examples/notes-web/notes.json</code></td>
                  </tr>
                  <tr>
                    <td>Response</td>
                    <td><code>200 · application/json</code></td>
                  </tr>
                  <tr>
                    <td>Request initiator</td>
                    <td><code>export.js</code> · script</td>
                  </tr>
                  <tr>
                    <td>Response structure</td>
                    <td>
                      <code>notes[]</code> with <code>id</code> and
                      <code>title</code> fields
                    </td>
                  </tr>
                </tbody>
              </table>
            </div>
            <p class="caption">
              The hosted example's request path includes the site's
              <code>/rea/</code> prefix.
            </p>
            <div class="code-block">
              <div class="code-header">
                <span>Read the loaded scripts</span
                ><button
                  class="copy-button"
                  type="button"
                  data-copy="browser-scripts"
                  aria-label="Copy read the loaded scripts"
                >
                  Copy
                </button>
              </div>
              <pre><code id="browser-scripts">npx -y rea-agents@latest inspect-web-page \
  http://127.0.0.1:9222 TARGET_ID \
  --include-script-sources --json</code></pre>
            </div>
            <p>
              The request identifies the data source, and REA records
              <code>export.js</code> as its initiator. Read the captured script
              source to see how the data is used:
            </p>
            <div class="code-block">
              <div class="code-header">
                <span>export.js · example source excerpt</span>
              </div>
              <pre><code>const response = await fetch(&quot;./notes.json&quot;);
const { notes } = await response.json();
// Format each note as a CSV row.
const url = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([csv], { type: &quot;text/csv&quot; }));
link.href = url;
link.download = &quot;notes.csv&quot;;
link.click();</code></pre>
            </div>
            <p>
              The download is constructed in the page using the JSON response.
              The CSV formatting step comes from the script; the network capture
              establishes that this click requested <code>notes.json</code>.
            </p>
            <p>
              <a href="../../examples/notes-web/">Open the example</a> ·
              <a href="../../examples/notes-web/export.js" download
                >Download export.js</a
              >
              ·
              <a href="../../examples/notes-web/notes.json" download
                >Download notes.json</a
              >
            </p>
            <blockquote class="prompt">
              <p>
                Find the script that requests <code>notes.json</code>. How does
                it escape titles containing commas or quotation marks?
              </p>
            </blockquote>
            <p>
              For an installed JavaScript or Electron app, continue with the
              <a href="../javascript/">application workflow</a> to follow files
              and process boundaries.
            </p>
          </section>
        </article>
      </div>
    </main>
    <footer class="site-footer">
      <div class="container footer-inner">
        <p>REA · Reverse Engineer Anything</p>
        <div class="footer-links">
          <a href="https://github.com/morluto/rea">Source</a
          ><a href="https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/LICENSE"
            >MIT license</a
          ><a href="https://discord.gg/GkcryMnJDM">Community</a>
        </div>
      </div>
    </footer>
    <p class="sr-only" id="copy-status" role="status" aria-live="polite"></p>

      <span aria-hidden="true">↑</span> Top
    </a>
  </body>
</html>
```

```html
                d="M20.317 4.3698a19.7913 19.7913 0 0 0-4.8851-1.5152.0741.0741 0 0 0-.0785.0371c-.211.3753-.4447.8648-.6083 1.2495-1.8447-.2762-3.68-.2762-5.4868 0-.1636-.3933-.4058-.8742-.6177-1.2495a.077.077 0 0 0-.0785-.037 19.7363 19.7363 0 0 0-4.8852 1.515.0699.0699 0 0 0-.0321.0277C.5334 9.0458-.319 13.5799.0992 18.0578a.0824.0824 0 0 0 .0312.0561c2.0528 1.5076 4.0413 2.4228 5.9929 3.0294a.0777.0777 0 0 0 .0842-.0276c.4616-.6304.8731-1.2952 1.226-1.9942a.076.076 0 0 0-.0416-.1057c-.6528-.2476-1.2743-.5495-1.8722-.8923a.077.077 0 0 1-.0076-.1277c.1258-.0943.2517-.1923.3718-.2914a.0743.0743 0 0 1 .0776-.0105c3.9278 1.7933 8.18 1.7933 12.0614 0a.0739.0739 0 0 1 .0785.0095c.1202.099.246.1981.3728.2924a.077.077 0 0 1-.0066.1276 12.2986 12.2986 0 0 1-1.873.8914.0766.0766 0 0 0-.0407.1067c.3604.698.7719 1.3628 1.225 1.9932a.076.076 0 0 0 .0842.0286c1.961-.6067 3.9495-1.5219 6.0023-3.0294a.077.077 0 0 0 .0313-.0552c.5004-5.177-.8382-9.6739-3.5485-13.6604a.061.061 0 0 0-.0312-.0286ZM8.02 15.3312c-1.1825 0-2.1569-1.0857-2.1569-2.419 0-1.3332.9555-2.4189 2.157-2.4189 1.2108 0 2.1757 1.0952 2.1568 2.419 0 1.3332-.9555 2.4189-2.1569 2.4189Zm7.9748 0c-1.1825 0-2.1569-1.0857-2.1569-2.419 0-1.3332.9554-2.4189 2.1569-2.4189 1.2108 0 2.1757 1.0952 2.1568 2.419 0 1.3332-.946 2.4189-2.1568 2.4189Z"
              />
            </svg>
```

```html
    </header>
    <main id="main" class="container">
      <div class="page-heading">
        <p class="breadcrumb">
          <a href="../../">Home</a> / <a href="../">Guides</a> / JavaScript
          &amp; Electron
        </p>
        <h1>Trace an Electron<br />CSV export.</h1>
        <p class="lede">
          Follow a button click from the page API, through Electron IPC, to the
          CSV file writer.
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="article-layout">
        <nav class="contents" aria-label="On this page">
          <p>In this guide</p>
          <ul>
            <li><a href="#example">The example</a></li>
            <li><a href="#ask">Ask your agent</a></li>
            <li><a href="#follow">Trace the export code</a></li>
            <li><a href="#try">Try the example</a></li>
            <li><a href="#next">Inspect the CSV writer</a></li>
          </ul>
        </nav>
        <article class="article" aria-label="JavaScript &amp; Electron">
          <section class="article-section" id="example">
            <h2>Where does “Export notes” go?</h2>
            <p>
              This guide uses a small Electron app. Clicking
              <strong>Export notes</strong> calls an API in the page, crosses
              into the main process, and writes a CSV. The behavior is spread
              across several files.
            </p>
            <figure class="workflow-figure">
              <p class="figure-title">
                The CSV export across Electron processes
              </p>
              <ol class="flow-steps">
                <li>
                  <span class="flow-label">Renderer → preload</span
                  ><span class="flow-node"><code>notes.exportCsv()</code></span
                  ><span class="flow-note"
                    ><code>renderer.js</code> calls the API exposed by
                    <code>preload.js</code>.</span
                  >
                </li>
                <li>
                  <span class="flow-label">Between processes</span
                  ><span class="flow-node"><code>notes:export</code></span
                  ><span class="flow-note"
                    >The preload invokes an IPC channel: a named message to the
                    main process.</span
                  >
                </li>
                <li>
                  <span class="flow-label">Main process</span
                  ><span class="flow-node">An export handler</span
                  ><span class="flow-note"
                    ><code>main.js</code> handles that channel and calls the CSV
                    writer.</span
                  >
                </li>
              </ol>
              <p class="flow-result">
                <code>csv.js</code> formats the notes →
                <code>main.js</code> writes <code>downloads/notes.csv</code>.
              </p>
              <figcaption>
                REA matches the literal IPC call to its handler and identifies
                the exposed API. The path is inferred from code; a runtime
                capture can check what executes.
              </figcaption>
            </figure>
          </section>
          <section class="article-section" id="ask">
            <h2>Ask about the CSV export</h2>
            <p>
              <a href="../../get-started/#agent">Connect your agent to REA</a>
              and give it the app directory or ASAR file:
            </p>
            <div class="agent-terminal">
              <div class="terminal-header">
                <span class="terminal-title"
                  ><span class="terminal-dots" aria-hidden="true"
                    ><i></i><i></i><i></i></span
                  >Your coding agent</span
                ><button
                  class="copy-button"
                  type="button"
                  data-copy="javascript-prompt"
                  aria-label="Copy example prompt"
                >
                  Copy
                </button>
              </div>
              <p class="terminal-prompt">
                <span class="prompt-symbol" aria-hidden="true">›</span
                ><span id="javascript-prompt"
                  >Use REA to find what happens when I export notes in this app.
                  Where is the CSV created?</span
                ><span class="terminal-cursor" aria-hidden="true"></span>
              </p>
            </div>
            <p class="caption">
              Example prompt. Include the absolute path to the application
              folder or <code>app.asar</code>.
            </p>
            <p>
              REA reads the application files and builds a map of entrypoints,
              modules and process boundaries. Your agent uses that map to narrow
              the investigation to the export feature.
            </p>
          </section>
          <section class="article-section" id="follow">
            <h2>Trace the export code</h2>
            <h3>The page calls a small API</h3>
            <div class="code-block">
              <div class="code-header">
                <span>renderer.js · example source</span>
              </div>
              <pre><code>document.querySelector(&quot;#export&quot;).addEventListener(&quot;click&quot;, async () =&gt; {
  const destination = await window.notes.exportCsv();
  document.querySelector(&quot;#status&quot;).textContent = `Saved to ${destination}`;
});</code></pre>
            </div>
            <p>
              The page knows the method name. The implementation lives in the
              preload, which exposes it to the renderer.
            </p>
            <div class="code-block">
              <div class="code-header">
                <span>preload.js · example source</span>
              </div>
              <pre><code>contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld(&quot;notes&quot;, {
  exportCsv: () =&gt; ipcRenderer.invoke(&quot;notes:export&quot;),
});</code></pre>
            </div>
            <p>
              REA records <code>notes.exportCsv</code> and the literal channel
              <code>notes:export</code>. It pairs that invocation with the
              single matching handler in the main process.
            </p>
            <div class="code-block">
              <div class="code-header">
                <span>main.js · example source</span>
              </div>
              <pre><code>ipcMain.handle(&quot;notes:export&quot;, () =&gt; {
  const destination = path.join(app.getPath(&quot;downloads&quot;), &quot;notes.csv&quot;);
  writeFileSync(destination, toCsv(notes), &quot;utf8&quot;);
  return destination;
});</code></pre>
            </div>
            <p>
              Reading the handler answers the original question:
              <code>csv.js</code> formats the notes, and the main process writes
              <code>notes.csv</code> into the user's Downloads folder.
            </p>
            <div class="code-block">
              <div class="code-header">
                <span>REA result · summary.ipc excerpt</span>
              </div>
              <pre><code>{
  &quot;literal_channels&quot;: 1,
  &quot;renderer_transmissions&quot;: 1,
  &quot;main_handlers&quot;: 1,
  &quot;paired_renderer_transmissions&quot;: 1,
  &quot;ambiguous_renderer_transmissions&quot;: 0
}</code></pre>
            </div>
            <p class="caption">
              Recorded by REA 4.1.0 on the downloadable example below. Source
              locations accompany the API, channel and handler findings.
            </p>
          </section>
          <section class="article-section" id="try">
            <h2>Analyze the example yourself</h2>
            <p>
              Download the example and unzip it. The archive contains the
              complete <code>notes-example</code> folder. Analyze it with
              Node.js and npm; Electron is not needed for this example.
            </p>
            <p>
              <a
                class="button"
                href="../../examples/notes-example.zip"
                download="notes-example.zip"
                >Download example ZIP</a
              >
            </p>
            <details class="evidence-details">
              <summary>Browse the six source files</summary>
              <ul class="example-files">
                <li>
                  <a href="../../examples/notes-electron/package.json" download
                    >package.json</a
                  >
                </li>
                <li>
                  <a href="../../examples/notes-electron/main.js" download
                    >main.js</a
                  >
                </li>
                <li>
                  <a href="../../examples/notes-electron/preload.js" download
                    >preload.js</a
                  >
                </li>
                <li>
                  <a href="../../examples/notes-electron/renderer.js" download
                    >renderer.js</a
                  >
                </li>
                <li>
                  <a href="../../examples/notes-electron/csv.js" download
                    >csv.js</a
                  >
                </li>
                <li>
                  <a href="../../examples/notes-electron/index.html" download
                    >index.html</a
                  >
                </li>
              </ul>
            </details>
            <div class="code-block">
              <div class="code-header">
                <span>Static application analysis</span
                ><button
                  class="copy-button"
                  type="button"
                  data-copy="javascript-command"
                  aria-label="Copy static application analysis"
                >
                  Copy
                </button>
              </div>
              <pre><code id="javascript-command">npx -y rea-agents@latest analyze-javascript-application \
  /absolute/path/to/notes-example --json</code></pre>
            </div>
            <p>
              Replace the path with the folder you unzipped. You should find one
              IPC channel and one matching handler in
              <code>normalized_result.summary.ipc</code>. Source locations are
              in <code>normalized_result.graph</code>.
            </p>
            <p>
              For your own app, use the same command with its directory or ASAR
              path. An agent can follow a literal string, API name or IPC
              channel with REA's feature tracing tools.
            </p>
          </section>
          <section class="article-section" id="next">
            <h2>Inspect the CSV writer</h2>
            <blockquote class="prompt">
              <p>
                Follow <code>notes:export</code> to its handler. Which inputs
                reach the CSV writer, and what happens if writing the file
                fails?
              </p>
            </blockquote>
            <p>
              Use the source locations to inspect those details. Computed
              channel names and ambiguous handlers can remain unresolved;
              runtime observations give you another way to investigate them.
            </p>
            <ul class="reading-list">
              <li>
                <a href="../../showcase/notion/"
                  >Follow Notion's clipboard bridge</a
                >
                <span>Apply the same approach to a packaged Electron app.</span>
              </li>

                ><span
                  >Capture a real click and see which request it makes.</span
                >
              </li>
              <li>
                <a href="../native/">Follow a native function</a
                ><span
                  >Continue into a binary when a feature depends on native
                  code.</span
                >
              </li>
            </ul>
          </section>
        </article>
```

```html
      <div class="page-heading">
        <p class="breadcrumb">
          <a href="../../">Home</a> / <a href="../">Guides</a> / Native analysis
        </p>
        <h1>Recover DX-Ball's<br />sound-pan calculation.</h1>
        <p class="lede">
          Inspect the original instructions, identify the input and constants,
          then check the recovered C.
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="article-layout">
        <nav class="contents" aria-label="On this page">
          <p>In this guide</p>
          <ul>
            <li><a href="#example">The example</a></li>
            <li><a href="#ask">Ask your agent</a></li>
            <li><a href="#follow">Read the REA results</a></li>
            <li><a href="#result">Recover and check</a></li>
            <li><a href="#try">Use your own binary</a></li>
          </ul>
        </nav>
        <article class="article" aria-label="Native analysis">
          <section class="article-section" id="example">
            <h2>Calculate left/right sound panning</h2>
            <p>
              In DX-Ball, a brick hit supplies a horizontal screen position. The
              sound code turns it into a left/right panning value.
            </p>
            <p>
              The starting function, <code>0x00406400</code>, has a short
              decompiler result: a call to <code>__ftol()</code>. REA also
              returns its instructions and callers, which give the agent a way
              to investigate the missing arithmetic.
            </p>
            <figure class="workflow-figure">
              <p class="figure-title">
                Three pieces of evidence, one calculation
              </p>
              <ol class="flow-steps">
                <li>
                  <span class="flow-label">01 · Instructions</span
                  ><span class="flow-node">An integer input</span
                  ><span class="flow-note"
                    >A stack read supplies the value used by the floating-point
                    instructions.</span
                  >
                </li>
                <li>
                  <span class="flow-label">02 · Caller</span
                  ><span class="flow-node">A screen coordinate</span
                  ><span class="flow-note"
                    >The brick-hit caller passes
                    <code>20 + 30 × tile_x</code>.</span
                  >
                </li>
                <li>
                  <span class="flow-label">03 · Data bytes</span
                  ><span class="flow-node">The numeric constants</span
                  ><span class="flow-note"
                    >Referenced bytes decode to <code>1.5625</code>,
                    <code>500.0</code> and a scale value.</span
                  >
                </li>
              </ol>
              <p class="flow-result">
                <code>pan = (x × 1.5625 − 500.0) × scale</code>
              </p>
              <figcaption>
                REA supplies the instructions, call relationship and bytes. The
                agent interprets them together.
              </figcaption>
            </figure>
          </section>
          <section class="article-section" id="ask">
            <h2>Ask about the behavior</h2>
            <p>
              After
              <a href="../../get-started/#agent">connecting REA to your agent</a
              >, provide the local executable and a question:
            </p>
            <div class="agent-terminal">
              <div class="terminal-header">
                <span class="terminal-title"
                  ><span class="terminal-dots" aria-hidden="true"
                    ><i></i><i></i><i></i></span
                  >Your coding agent</span
                ><button
                  class="copy-button"
                  type="button"
                  data-copy="native-prompt"
                  aria-label="Copy example prompt"
                >
                  Copy
                </button>
              </div>
              <p class="terminal-prompt">
                <span class="prompt-symbol" aria-hidden="true">›</span
                ><span id="native-prompt"
                  >Use REA to find how DX-Ball calculates sound panning. Explain
                  the calculation and show the code.</span
                ><span class="terminal-cursor" aria-hidden="true"></span>
              </p>
            </div>
            <p class="caption">
              Example prompt. Give your agent the path to your local DX-Ball
              1.07 executable.
            </p>
          </section>
          <section class="article-section" id="follow">
            <h2>Read the REA results</h2>
            <h3>Read the input</h3>
            <div class="code-block">
              <div class="code-header">
                <span>REA instruction excerpt · 0x406409</span>
              </div>
              <pre><code>MOV EAX, dword ptr [EBP + 0x8]
MOV dword ptr [EBP + -0xc], EAX
FILD dword ptr [EBP + -0xc]</code></pre>
            </div>
            <p>
              The instructions load an integer argument and convert it for
              floating-point arithmetic. This is the input absent from the first
              pseudocode view.
            </p>
            <h3 class="small-heading">Follow the caller</h3>
            <div class="code-block">
              <div class="code-header">
                <span>REA caller excerpt · 0x411f5b</span>
              </div>
              <pre><code>ADD EAX, 0x14
PUSH EAX
CALL 0x00406400</code></pre>
            </div>
            <p>
              REA identifies the brick-hit caller. Its earlier instructions
              multiply the tile coordinate by 30; adding <code>0x14</code> (20)
              gives the brick's screen position.
            </p>
            <h3 class="small-heading">Read the referenced constants</h3>
            <div class="code-block">
              <div class="code-header">
                <span
                  >REA byte results · interpreted as little-endian doubles</span
                >
              </div>
              <pre><code>0x420068  000000000000f93f  → 1.5625
0x420070  0000000000407f40  → 500.0
0x4210a0  000000000000f03f  → 1.0</code></pre>
            </div>
            <p>
              The arithmetic references these addresses. Reading the bytes
              supplies the actual values; the instruction order tells the agent
              how they are used.
            </p>
          </section>
          <section class="article-section" id="result">
            <h2>Write and check the recovered function</h2>
            <div class="code-block">
              <div class="code-header"><span>Recovered C · excerpt</span></div>
              <pre><code>pan = (double)x;
pan = pan * 1.5625;
pan = pan - 500.0;
pan = pan * dxball_pan_scale;
return (DxBallInt)pan;</code></pre>
            </div>
            <p>
              With a scale of 1.0, screen positions 0, 320 and 640 map to −500,
              0 and 500 before integer conversion. The calculation puts the
              center of the screen at the center of the stereo field.
            </p>
            <p>
              The agent used REA's findings to write the C. Separate checks
              compared 3,205 inputs against the original x86 function and
              reproduced all 63 compiled bytes of the complete function.
            </p>
            <p>
              <a href="../../showcase/dx-ball/#sound-pan"
                >See the full investigation and assembly-to-C comparison</a
              >
            </p>
          </section>
          <section class="article-section" id="try">
            <h2>Try it with your own binary</h2>
            <p>
              <a href="../../get-started/#native"
                >Connect a native analysis provider</a
              >, then give your agent a local executable or library and a
              feature to investigate. Useful starting questions include “How is
              this file parsed?” or “Which function handles this menu action?”
            </p>
            <p>
              If you already know a function name or address, you can query it
              from the terminal. For a configured Ghidra installation:
            </p>
            <div class="code-block">
              <div class="code-header">
                <span>Function analysis</span
                ><button
                  class="copy-button"
                  type="button"
                  data-copy="native-command"
                  aria-label="Copy function analysis"
                >
                  Copy
                </button>
              </div>
              <pre><code id="native-command">npx -y rea-agents@latest function /absolute/path/to/program main \
  --provider ghidra --json</code></pre>
            </div>
            <p>
              Replace the target path and <code>main</code> with your own
              function name or address. Each CLI invocation imports and analyzes
              the binary, then closes its session. Your agent's MCP queries
              reuse the imported binary while that session is open.
            </p>
            <p>
              Read the pseudocode alongside instructions and references. When a
              result leaves a call or value unresolved, use that location as the
              next question.
            </p>
          </section>
        </article>
      </div>
    </main>
    <footer class="site-footer">
      <div class="container footer-inner">
        <p>REA · Reverse Engineer Anything</p>
        <div class="footer-links">

      <span aria-hidden="true">↑</span> Top
    </a>
  </body>
</html>

```

```html
      <section class="section" id="what-is-re">
        <div class="container">
          <div class="home-definition">
            <h2>What is reverse engineering?</h2>
            <p class="lede">
              Finding out how software works by
              <strong>examining the program itself.</strong>
            </p>
          </div>
          <p class="home-purpose">
            The goal: understand a feature well enough to
            <mark class="prose-highlight">explain it</mark>,
            <mark class="prose-highlight">change it</mark> or
            <mark class="prose-highlight">rebuild it.</mark>
          </p>
          <p class="comparison-question">
            One question:
            <strong>why does Calculator give 220 for 200 + 10%?</strong>
          </p>
          <figure class="home-role-comparison" id="how-rea-helps">
            <div
              class="manual-investigation step-comparison"

                <strong class="prose-highlight">yourself</strong>

                <aside
                  class="expert-reasoning"
                  aria-label="Illustrative expert reasoning"
                >
                  <div
                    id="expert-reasoning"
                    aria-live="polite"
                    aria-atomic="true"

                    <div class="expert-thought" data-step-note="1">
                      <p class="thought-label">01 · Which branch?</p>
                      <p>
                        “<strong>0x5b? 0x5c?</strong> Two jumps to the same
                        place. Which operators are these?”
                      </p>
                      <p class="expert-task">
                        Look up the command IDs, then label the branch.
                      </p>
                      <dl class="expert-facts">
                        <div>
                          <dt>0x5b</dt>
                          <dd>Divide ÷</dd>
                        </div>
                        <div>
                          <dt>0x5c</dt>
                          <dd>Multiply ×</dd>
                        </div>
                      </dl>
                    </div>
                    <div class="expert-thought" data-step-note="2">
                      <p class="thought-label">02 · What do the calls do?</p>
                      <p>
                        “100 is clear. The calls are just addresses.
                        <strong>Which one divides? Which value goes in?</strong
                        >”
                      </p>
                      <p class="expert-task">
                        Inspect the helpers and trace the stored values.
                      </p>
                      <dl class="expert-facts">
                        <div>
                          <dt>0x64</dt>
                          <dd>100</dd>
                        </div>
                        <div>
                          <dt>…123190</dt>
                          <dd>Divide</dd>
                        </div>
                      </dl>
                    </div>
                    <div class="expert-thought" data-step-note="3">
                      <p class="thought-label">03 · What is the rule?</p>
                      <p>
                        “This path multiplies by the other input. So
                        <strong>10% means 10% of 200</strong> after +.”
                      </p>
                      <p class="expert-task">
                        Name the operands and check both operator paths.
                      </p>
                      <div class="expert-rule">
                        <span>200 × 10 / 100</span>
                        <strong>20</strong>
                      </div>
                    </div>

                <strong
                  >You decode the instructions, follow the calls and reconstruct
                  the calculation.</strong
                >
              </p>
            </div>

                With REA · You ask
                <strong class="prose-highlight">your agent</strong>
              </p>

                    <strong>a percentage of the first number.</strong>

                    <code>10% of 200 = 20</code><span aria-hidden="true">↓</span
                    ><strong>200 + 20 = 220</strong>

              <dd>
                Rebuild the game with
                <mark class="prose-highlight">adjustable speed.</mark>

            <div>
              <dt>Why reverse engineer it?</dt>
              <dd>
                To reproduce its acceleration, we need
                <strong>the rule in the running game</strong>: how fast it
                starts, how much it increases and when it stops.
              </dd>

              <li>
                <span class="flow-label">01 · REA</span

              </li>
              <li>

                  pace.</span
                >
              </li>
```
