```html
            <summary>
              See the script, checks and how to try the analysis
            </summary>
            <p>
              REA inspected the HTTP browser edition through a local debugging
              connection and returned the loaded <code>index.js</code>,
              including its source and digest.
            </p>
            <div class="code-block">
              <div class="code-header">
                <span>Selected settings from the inspected script</span>
              </div>
              <pre><code>ACCELERATION: 0.001,
MAX_SPEED: 13,
SPEED: 6</code></pre>

            <p>
              We called the original game’s update function in a controlled
              browser check, with obstacles and automatic scheduling disabled.
              After 4,000 updates, speed was 10.0; after 10,000, it was 13.0,
              rounded to one decimal.
            </p>
            <p>
              The new mini-game keeps that speed rule. Its drawing, jumping and
              collision code are a small teaching implementation.

              endpoint, then copy the prompt above.

      <section class="section" id="calculator">
        <div class="container">
          <div class="section-heading">
            <p class="eyebrow">Example 02 · Windows Calculator</p>
            <h2>Rebuild Calculator’s % button.</h2>
            <p class="lede">
              We saw why <strong>200 + 10% gives 220.</strong> Now let’s recover
              the rules for both + and ×, and try them.
            </p>
          </div>
          <dl class="case-brief">
            <div>
              <dt>Goal</dt>
              <dd>
                Build a small calculator that handles
                <mark class="prose-highlight">both + and × correctly.</mark>
              </dd>
            </div>
            <div>
              <dt>Why reverse engineer it?</dt>
              <dd>
                The same button uses
                <strong>different rules after + and ×.</strong> We inspect the
                installed app to find which number the percentage is applied to.
              </dd>
            </div>
          </dl>
          <div class="home-example-grid">
            <figure class="percent-figure" data-percent-demo>
              <p class="figure-title">Try the calculation</p>
              <div
                class="percent-operation"
                role="group"
                aria-label="Choose the calculation"
                hidden
              >
                <button
                  type="button"
                  data-percent-operation="add"
                  aria-pressed="true"
                >
                  200 + 10%
                </button>
                <button
                  type="button"
                  data-percent-operation="multiply"
                  aria-pressed="false"
                >
                  200 × 10%
                </button>
              </div>
              <div class="percent-display">
                <span class="percent-expression" data-percent-expression
                  >200 +</span
                >
                <strong data-percent-display>20</strong>
              </div>
              <div class="percent-controls" hidden>
                <button
                  type="button"
                  class="percent-key"
                  data-percent-key="percent"
                >
                  %
                </button>
                <button
                  type="button"
                  class="percent-key"
                  data-percent-key="equals"
                  disabled
                >
                  =
                </button>
                <button
                  type="button"
                  class="percent-reset"
                  data-percent-key="reset"
                >
                  Reset
                </button>
              </div>
              <p class="percent-status" data-percent-status role="status">
                10% of 200 = 20. Then 200 + 20 = 220.
              </p>
              <figcaption>
                Interactive illustration of the inspected percentage rule.
              </figcaption>
            </figure>
            <div class="percent-explanation">
              <div class="rea-finding">
                <p class="finding-label">REA returned</p>
                <p>
                  <strong
                    >One branch divides by 100. The other also multiplies by the
                    first number.</strong
                  >
                  The agent uses both to recreate the % button.
                </p>
              </div>
              <p>
                For this example, <code>previous = 200</code> and
                <code>current = 10</code>.
              </p>
              <div class="agent-terminal">
                <div class="terminal-header">
                  <span class="terminal-title"
                    ><span class="terminal-dots" aria-hidden="true"
                      ><i></i><i></i><i></i></span
                    >Example prompt · Rebuild the % button</span
                  >
                  <button
                    class="copy-button"
                    type="button"
                    data-copy="calculator-analysis-prompt"
                    aria-label="Copy Calculator analysis prompt"
                  >
                    Copy
                  </button>
                </div>
                <p class="terminal-prompt">
                  <span class="prompt-symbol" aria-hidden="true">›</span
                  ><span id="calculator-analysis-prompt"
                    >Use REA to inspect Windows Calculator’s % button. Recover
                    the rules after + and ×, then build a small calculator that
                    uses both.</span
                  ><span class="terminal-cursor" aria-hidden="true"></span>
                </p>
              </div>
              <div class="code-block">
                <div class="code-header">
                  <span>Readable summary of the % handler</span>
                </div>
                <pre><code>if (operation == multiply || operation == divide) {
  percent = current / 100;
} else {
  <span class="code-key">percent = current * previous / 100;</span>
}</code></pre>
              </div>
              <dl class="percent-rules">
                <div>
                  <dt>With +</dt>
                  <dd>
                    <strong>Take 10% of the first number.</strong
                    ><code>10% of 200 = 20 → 200 + 20 = 220</code>
                  </dd>
                </div>
                <div>
                  <dt>With ×</dt>
                  <dd>
                    <strong>Turn 10% into 0.1.</strong
                    ><code>200 × 0.1 = 20</code>
                  </dd>
                </div>
              </dl>
            </div>
          </div>
          <figure class="workflow-figure calculator-trace">
            <p class="figure-title">
              From the installed app to a working % button
            </p>
            <ol class="flow-steps">
              <li>
                <span class="flow-label">01 · REA reads calc.exe</span
                ><span class="flow-node">It launches the Calculator app</span
                ><span class="flow-note"
                  >The code opens <code>ms-calculator:</code>. The agent then
                  selects the installed app’s library.</span
                >
              </li>
              <li>
                <span class="flow-label">02 · REA reads the library</span
                ><span class="flow-node">Return the % handler’s code</span
                ><span class="flow-note"
                  >The function checks the operator and uses the constant
                  <code>100</code>.</span
                >
              </li>
              <li>
                <span class="flow-label">03 · Your agent interprets it</span
                ><span class="flow-node">Explain and reproduce the rules</span
                ><span class="flow-note"
                  >Crosscheck the branch with Microsoft’s source, then try + and
                  × above.</span
                >
              </li>
            </ol>
          </figure>
          <details class="home-evidence-details">
            <summary>See the real code and how the answer was checked</summary>

            <div class="code-comparison">
              <div class="code-block">
                <div class="code-header">
                  <span>REA · selected original instructions</span>
                </div>
                <pre><code>0x180124945: MOV EAX, dword ptr [R13 + 0x18]
0x180124949: <span class="code-key">CMP EAX, 0x5c</span>
0x18012494c: JZ 0x180124aba
0x180124952: <span class="code-key">CMP EAX, 0x5b</span>
0x180124955: JZ 0x180124aba
0x18012495b: <span class="code-key">MOV EDX, 0x64</span></code></pre>
              </div>
              <div class="code-block">
                <div class="code-header">
                  <span>Operator IDs · Microsoft’s source</span>
                </div>
                <pre><code>#define IDC_MUL 92      // 0x5c
#define IDC_DIV 91      // 0x5b
#define IDC_PERCENT 118 // 0x76

0x64 = 100</code></pre>
              </div>
            </div>

            <p class="caption">
              Inspected with REA 4.1.0: Windows Calculator 11.2508.4.0, x64. The
              readable summary uses names from Microsoft’s public source to
              explain the recovered branch.
            </p>
            <p class="caption">
              <a
                href="https://github.com/microsoft/calculator/blob/d125246a4e19842ce1332e6c7839cf0e110027d8/src/CalcManager/CEngine/scifunc.cpp#L98-L111"
                >Percentage implementation</a
              >
              ·
              <a
                href="https://github.com/microsoft/calculator/blob/d125246a4e19842ce1332e6c7839cf0e110027d8/src/CalculatorUnitTests/CalculatorManagerTest.cpp#L350-L370"
                >Microsoft’s test cases</a
              >
              · <a href="guides/native/">Native setup guide</a>
            </p>
          </details>
        </div>
      </section>
```

```html
        <p class="breadcrumb">

        <p class="eyebrow">Case study · Aegis Authenticator</p>
        <h1>How does an authenticator<br />generate a login code?</h1>
        <p class="lede">
          A six-digit code changes every 30 seconds. Use REA to find the
          calculation in an Android APK, then rebuild it with a clock you can
          control.
        </p>
        <p class="page-meta">
          Aegis 3.4.3 · Android · Official release APK · 6.9 MB
        </p>
        <a class="text-link" href="https://github.com/beemdevelopment/Aegis"
          >View Aegis on GitHub</a
        >
      </div>

      <figure class="workflow-figure case-figure">
        <p class="figure-title">From an APK to a code you can reproduce</p>
        <ol class="flow-steps">
          <li>
            <span class="flow-label">01 · Locate the feature</span
            ><strong class="flow-node"
              >3,077 classes → generating methods</strong
            ><span class="flow-note"
              >REA searches the package and traces the code used by the display
              and copy actions.</span
            >
          </li>
          <li>
            <span class="flow-label">02 · Read the calculation</span
            ><strong class="flow-node">Time + account key → six digits</strong
            ><span class="flow-note"
              >REA returns the methods and defaults. The agent explains how they
              fit together.</span
            >
          </li>
          <li>
            <span class="flow-label">03 · Rebuild and check</span
            ><strong class="flow-node">Change the clock. Watch the code.</strong
            ><span class="flow-note"
              >A new browser demo reproduces the rule and checks it against
              public reference cases.</span
            >
          </li>
        </ol>
      </figure>

            <h2>Ask your agent</h2>
            <p>
              The app shows a changing login code. We want to find
              <strong>what makes it change</strong> and reproduce that behavior.
            </p>
            <div class="agent-terminal">
              <div class="terminal-header">
                <span class="terminal-title"
                  ><span class="terminal-dots" aria-hidden="true"
                    ><i></i><i></i><i></i></span

                  class="copy-button"
                  type="button"

                  aria-label="Copy Aegis example prompt"
                >
                  Copy
                </button>
              </div>
              <p class="terminal-prompt">
                <span class="prompt-symbol" aria-hidden="true">›</span
                ><span id="aegis-prompt"
                  >Use REA to inspect aegis-v3.4.3.apk. Find how it generates
                  the six-digit login code, explain why it changes every 30
                  seconds, and rebuild a small demo where I can change the
                  time.</span
                ><span class="terminal-cursor" aria-hidden="true"></span>
              </p>

          <section class="article-section" id="demo">
            <h2>Try the code generator</h2>
            <p>
              The app groups time into
              <mark class="prose-highlight">30-second blocks.</mark> It combines
              the block number with the account key to generate a code. The same
              key and block produce the same code.
            </p>
            <figure class="workflow-figure aegis-demo" data-aegis-demo>
              <p class="figure-title">Move the clock across 60 seconds</p>
              <ol class="flow-steps aegis-calculation">
                <li>
                  <span class="flow-label">Time</span
                  ><strong class="flow-node"
                    ><output data-aegis-seconds>59</output> seconds</strong
                  ><span class="flow-note">Our adjustable example clock</span>
                </li>
                <li>
                  <span class="flow-label">30-second block</span
                  ><strong class="flow-node"
                    >Block <output data-aegis-block>1</output></strong
                  ><span class="flow-note"
                    ><code data-aegis-division>floor(59 / 30)</code><br /><span
                      data-aegis-window
                      >30–59 seconds</span
                    ></span
                  >
                </li>
                <li>
                  <span class="flow-label">Generated code</span
                  ><strong class="flow-node aegis-code"
                    ><output
                      data-aegis-code
                      aria-live="polite"
                      aria-atomic="true"
                      >287082</output
                    ></strong
                  ><span class="flow-note"
                    >Account key + block → six digits</span
                  >
                </li>
              </ol>
              <div class="aegis-clock-controls">
                <label for="aegis-clock">Example time, in seconds</label>
                <input
                  id="aegis-clock"
                  type="range"
                  min="0"
                  max="120"
                  step="1"
                  value="59"
                  disabled
                />
                <div class="aegis-clock-scale" aria-hidden="true">
                  <span>0</span><span>30</span><span>60</span><span>90</span
                  ><span>120</span>
                </div>
                <div class="actions">
                  <button
                    class="button secondary"
                    type="button"
                    data-aegis-time="59"
                    disabled
                  >
                    59 seconds</button
                  ><button
                    class="button secondary"
                    type="button"
                    data-aegis-time="60"
                    disabled
                  >
                    60 seconds
                  </button>
                </div>
                <p class="caption">
                  At 59 seconds: <strong>287082.</strong> At 60 seconds:
                  <strong>359152.</strong> Moving within one block leaves the
                  code unchanged.
                </p>
                <p class="caption" data-aegis-status role="status"></p>
              </div>
              <figcaption>
                The key is fixed, public
                <a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6238.html#appendix-B"
                  >RFC 6238 test data</a
                >. The demo implements the calculation recovered from the APK.
              </figcaption>
              <noscript

                </p></noscript

          <section class="article-section" id="find">
            <h2>Find the code with REA</h2>
            <ol class="rea-queries">
              <li>
                <h4>Narrow the APK to three classes</h4>
                <div class="rea-query-pair">
                  <div class="code-block">
                    <div class="code-header"><span>Agent → REA</span></div>
                    <pre><code>inspect_android_package
{"path": "aegis-v3.4.3.apk"}

search_android_classes
{"path": "aegis-v3.4.3.apk",
 "query": "Totp"}</code></pre>
                  </div>
                  <div class="code-block">
                    <div class="code-header">
                      <span>REA → agent · selected results</span>
                    </div>
                    <pre><code>Package: com.beemdevelopment.aegis
Version: 3.4.3
Classes: 3,077

Three matches:
  otp.TotpInfo
  ui.views.TotpProgressBar
  importers.TotpAuthenticatorImporter</code></pre>
                  </div>
                </div>
                <p>
                  <code>TotpInfo</code> is the calculation candidate; the other
                  two concern the progress bar and imported accounts. TOTP means
                  a time-based one-time password.
                </p>
              </li>
              <li>
                <h4>Connect the generator to the app's display</h4>
                <div class="rea-query-pair">
                  <div class="code-block">
                    <div class="code-header"><span>Agent → REA</span></div>
                    <pre><code>inspect_android_class
{"path": "aegis-v3.4.3.apk",
 "class_name":
  "com.beemdevelopment.aegis.otp.TotpInfo"}

trace_android_references
{"path": "aegis-v3.4.3.apk",
 "class_name":
  "com.beemdevelopment.aegis.otp.OtpInfo",
 "method_name": "getOtp"}</code></pre>
                  </div>
                  <div class="code-block">
                    <div class="code-header">
                      <span>REA → agent · methods and callers</span>
                    </div>
                    <pre><code>TotpInfo methods:
  getOtp()      · overload 0
  getOtp(long)  · overload 1

OtpInfo.getOtp callers:
  ui.views.EntryHolder.getOtp
  ui.MainActivity.copyEntryCode</code></pre>
                  </div>
                </div>
                <p>
                  REA identifies the timestamp overload and finds the base
                  method's callers. Inspecting
                  <code>EntryHolder.getOtp</code> then shows the display calling
                  <code>TotpInfo.getOtp(timestamp)</code>.
                </p>
              </li>
            </ol>
            <p class="caption">
              Requests show a shortened input path. Result class names omit the
              common <code>com.beemdevelopment.aegis</code> prefix.
            </p>
          </section>

          <section class="article-section" id="calculation">
            <h2>Read the calculation</h2>
            <p>
              REA returns
              <strong
                >the clock conversion, default settings and generating
                methods.</strong
              >
              The constructors set a 30-second interval and six digits; the
              timestamp method turns seconds into a block number.
            </p>
            <div class="step-comparison" data-step-comparison>
              <div
                class="step-selector aegis-step-selector"
                role="group"
                aria-label="Follow the login-code calculation"
              >
                <button
                  type="button"
                  data-select-step="1"
                  aria-pressed="true"
                  aria-controls="aegis-java aegis-summary"
                >
                  <span>01</span> Time block
                </button>
                <button
                  type="button"
                  data-select-step="2"
                  aria-pressed="false"
                  aria-controls="aegis-java aegis-summary"
                >
                  <span>02</span> Key + block
                </button>
                <button
                  type="button"
                  data-select-step="3"
                  aria-pressed="false"
                  aria-controls="aegis-java aegis-summary"
                >
                  <span>03</span> Six digits
                </button>
              </div>
              <div class="code-comparison">
                <div class="code-block">
                  <div class="code-header">
                    <span>REA · selected decompiled Java</span>
                  </div>
                  <pre><code id="aegis-java"><span class="code-step is-active" data-step="1">// TotpInfo defaults and clock
setPeriod(30);
getOtp(System.currentTimeMillis() / 1000);

// OtpInfo default algorithm and digits
this(bArr, "SHA1", 6);

// Block passed to the generator
(long) Math.floor(j / ((double) this._period))</span>

<span class="code-step" data-step="2">// generateOTP → getHash
byte[] hash = getHash(bArr, str, j);

// getHash: account key + encoded block
Mac mac = Mac.getInstance(str);
mac.init(secretKeySpec);
return mac.doFinal(bArrArray);</span>

<span class="code-step" data-step="3">// OTP.toString, case 0
this._code % ((int) Math.pow(10.0d, i))

// Keep leading zeroes
while (sb.length() &lt; i) {
    sb.insert(0, "0");
}</span></code></pre>
                </div>
                <div class="code-block">
                  <div class="code-header">
                    <span>Readable summary · agent's interpretation</span>
                  </div>
                  <pre><code id="aegis-summary"><span class="code-step is-active" data-step="1">// Group time into 30-second blocks
seconds = current_time_ms / 1000
block = floor(seconds / 30)</span>

<span class="code-step" data-step="2">// Generate a number from the key and block
hash = HMAC_SHA1(account_key,
                 big_endian_8_bytes(block))
number = select_31_bits(hash)</span>

<span class="code-step" data-step="3">// Format the default six-digit code
code = number % 1_000_000
code = pad_with_zeroes(code, 6)</span></code></pre>
                </div>
              </div>
              <div class="step-detail" data-step-note="1">
                <p>
                  <strong>Time chooses the block.</strong> Seconds 30 through 59
                  all give block 1. At 60 seconds, the block becomes 2.
                </p>
              </div>
              <div class="step-detail" data-step-note="2">
                <p>
                  <strong>The key matters too.</strong> The generator combines
                  the account key with the block. An account with a different
                  key can show a different code at the same time.
                </p>
              </div>
              <div class="step-detail" data-step-note="3">
                <p>
                  <strong>Keep six digits.</strong> The remainder after division
                  by 1,000,000 is padded with zeroes when needed, so a code can
                  begin with 0.
                </p>
              </div>
            </div>
            <p class="caption">
              Excerpts from several inspected methods, with line wrapping for
              display. The right panel is an explanatory summary.
              <a
                href="https://github.com/beemdevelopment/Aegis/blob/d6f4e5925a97e4e91593f1542085eae03432a759/LICENSE"
                >Aegis code is GPL-3.0.</a
              >
            </p>
            <details class="evidence-details">
              <summary>Inside the generator</summary>
              <p>
                The released APK puts <code>generateOTP</code> in
                <code>kotlin.ExceptionsKt</code>. REA follows the call from
                <code>TotpInfo</code> and returns this body; the original source
                calls the helper <code>HOTP</code>.
              </p>
              <div class="code-block">
                <div class="code-header">
                  <span>REA · generateOTP, complete body</span>
                </div>
                <pre><code>public static OTP generateOTP(byte[] bArr, String str,
        int i, long j)
        throws NoSuchAlgorithmException, InvalidKeyException {
    byte[] hash = getHash(bArr, str, j);
    int i2 = hash[hash.length - 1] &amp; 15;
    return new OTP(
        (hash[i2 + 3] &amp; 255)
        | ((hash[i2] &amp; 127) &lt;&lt; 24)
        | ((hash[i2 + 1] &amp; 255) &lt;&lt; 16)
        | ((hash[i2 + 2] &amp; 255) &lt;&lt; 8), i, 0);
}</code></pre>
              </div>
              <p>
                The last hash byte selects a position. Four bytes at that
                position provide a positive 31-bit number; formatting reduces it
                to the requested number of digits. The constructor's last
                argument selects the code-formatting branch introduced by
                compilation.
              </p>
              <p>
                <a
                  href="https://github.com/beemdevelopment/Aegis/blob/d6f4e5925a97e4e91593f1542085eae03432a759/app/src/main/java/com/beemdevelopment/aegis/crypto/otp/HOTP.java"
                  >Compare with the matching release source</a
                >.
              </p>
            </details>
          </section>

          <section class="article-section" id="verify">
            <h2>Check the reconstruction</h2>
            <p>
              We assembled the selected REA-returned Java methods in a small
              test program. Their output matched an independent reconstruction
              on <strong>133 test cases</strong>, including time-block
              boundaries and codes beginning with zero.
            </p>
            <div class="evidence-table-wrap">
              <table class="evidence-table">
                <thead>
                  <tr>
                    <th>Example time</th>
                    <th>Block</th>
                    <th>Six-digit code</th>
                  </tr>
                </thead>
                <tbody>
                  <tr>
                    <td>30 seconds</td>
                    <td>1</td>
                    <td><code>287082</code></td>
                  </tr>
                  <tr>
                    <td>59 seconds</td>
                    <td>1</td>
                    <td><code>287082</code></td>
                  </tr>
                  <tr>
                    <td>60 seconds</td>
                    <td>2</td>
                    <td><code>359152</code></td>
                  </tr>
                  <tr>
                    <td>1,111,111,109 seconds</td>
                    <td>37,037,036</td>
                    <td><code>081804</code></td>
                  </tr>
                </tbody>
              </table>
            </div>
            <p>
              The generator also matches the six published SHA-1 reference cases
              in
              <a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6238.html#appendix-B"
                >RFC 6238</a
              >. Check the browser implementation against them:
            </p>
            <div class="actions">
              <button
                class="button secondary"
                type="button"
                data-aegis-check
                disabled
              >
                Run reference checks</button
              ><a class="text-link" href="../../assets/aegis-otp.js"
                >Read the demo's calculation</a
              >
            </div>
            <p
              class="caption"
              data-aegis-check-result
              role="status"
              aria-live="polite"
            >
              The reference cases use eight digits. The check also verifies
              their six-digit results.
            </p>
            <p class="caption">
              Verification runs extracted Java methods and the new demo. The
              Android APK was inspected statically.
            </p>
          </section>

          <section class="article-section" id="try">
            <h2>Inspect the APK yourself</h2>
            <p>
              <a href="../../get-started/">Set up REA</a> on macOS or Linux,
              then download these two files into the same folder. On Windows,
              use a Linux environment such as WSL.
            </p>
            <p>
              Android analysis needs a full JDK 17 or later. Select it with
              <code>JAVA_HOME</code> or <code>PATH</code>. This case used JDK
              21.
            </p>
            <div class="actions">
              <a
                class="button"
                href="https://github.com/beemdevelopment/Aegis/releases/download/v3.4.3/aegis-v3.4.3.apk"
                >Download Aegis APK</a
              ><a
                class="text-link"
                href="https://github.com/1013503897/jadx-headless-mcp/releases/download/v0.7.1/jadx-headless-mcp-0.7.1-all.jar"
                >Download Android analysis provider</a
              >
            </div>
            <p>Point REA at the provider file and inspect the APK:</p>
            <div class="code-block">
              <div class="code-header">
                <span>macOS / Linux</span
                ><button
                  class="copy-button"
                  type="button"
                  data-copy="aegis-inspect-command"
                  aria-label="Copy APK inspection command"
                >
                  Copy
                </button>
              </div>
              <pre><code id="aegis-inspect-command">REA_JADX_MCP_JAR="$PWD/jadx-headless-mcp-0.7.1-all.jar" \
npx rea-agents@latest inspect-android-package \
  ./aegis-v3.4.3.apk --format json --full-output</code></pre>
            </div>
            <p>
              Your agent can continue through REA's CLI using the prompt above.
              For MCP, add <code>REA_JADX_MCP_JAR</code> to the REA server's
              environment and reconnect it.
            </p>
            <p>
              A next question:
              <strong
                >what happens when an account uses eight digits or a different
                time interval?</strong
              >
            </p>
          </section>
```

```html
        <p class="eyebrow">Case study · DownUnderCTF 2023</p>
        <h1>Find the flag in<br />a CTF binary.</h1>
        <p class="lede">
          Use REA to inspect a small flag checker, turn its rules into equations
          and find an input that makes the original program print
          <code>Correct!</code>.
        </p>
        <p class="page-meta">
          masked squares flag checker · Easy · Linux x86-64
        </p>
        <a
          class="text-link"
          href="https://github.com/DownUnderCTF/Challenges_2023_Public/tree/b48f83db2984bc7fa2ec7879a32d7efb1be8d333/rev/masked-squares-flag-checker"
          >View the original challenge</a
        >
      </div>

      <figure class="workflow-figure case-figure">
        <p class="figure-title">From a binary to a checked answer</p>
        <ol class="flow-steps">
          <li>
            <span class="flow-label">01 · Find the check</span
            ><strong class="flow-node">Strings → checking functions</strong
            ><span class="flow-note"
              >REA finds the prompt, its references and the code that accepts or
              rejects an input.</span
            >
          </li>
          <li>
            <span class="flow-label">02 · Extract the rules</span
            ><strong class="flow-node">36 characters · 26 sums</strong
            ><span class="flow-note"
              >REA returns the instructions and data behind each check. The
              agent turns them into equations.</span
            >
          </li>
          <li>
            <span class="flow-label">03 · Solve and run</span
            ><strong class="flow-node">Recovered flag → Correct!</strong
            ><span class="flow-note"
              >A Python script solves the equations. REA captures the original
              program accepting the result.</span
            >
          </li>
        </ol>
        <figcaption>
          The challenge is by joseph, published in DownUnderCTF's official
          repository.
        </figcaption>
      </figure>

        <article class="article" aria-label="CTF flag-checker case study">
          <section class="article-section" id="find">
            <h2>Find the checking code</h2>
            <p>
              The handout is a 15 KB executable. It asks for a flag, then prints
              <code>Correct!</code> or <code>Incorrect!</code>. Start with a
              simple request to your agent.
            </p>
            <div class="agent-terminal">
              <div class="terminal-header">
                <span class="terminal-title"
                  ><span class="terminal-dots" aria-hidden="true"
                    ><i></i><i></i><i></i></span
                  >Your coding agent</span
                >
                <button
                  class="copy-button"
                  type="button"
                  data-copy="ctf-prompt"
                  aria-label="Copy CTF example prompt"
                >
                  Copy
                </button>
              </div>
              <p class="terminal-prompt">
                <span class="prompt-symbol" aria-hidden="true">›</span
                ><span id="ctf-prompt"
                  >Use REA to analyze ms_flag_checker and find the flag. Explain
                  how the checks work, then verify the answer with the original
                  program.</span
                ><span class="terminal-cursor" aria-hidden="true"></span>
              </p>
            </div>
            <p class="caption">
              An example prompt, with the downloaded challenge available locally
              and a native analysis provider connected.
            </p>
            <ol class="rea-queries">
              <li>
                <h4>Follow the input prompt to its function</h4>
                <div class="rea-query-pair">
                  <div class="code-block">
                    <div class="code-header"><span>Agent → REA</span></div>
                    <pre><code>open_binary
{"path": "ms_flag_checker"}

search_strings
{"pattern": "flag|correct|wrong|input",
 "mode": "regex", "case_sensitive": false}

xrefs
{"address": "0x102004"}

resolve_containing_procedure
{"address": "0x10126d"}</code></pre>
                  </div>
                  <div class="code-block">
                    <div class="code-header">
                      <span>REA → agent · selected results</span>
                    </div>
                    <pre><code>0x102004  "What is the flag? "
0x10201c  "Incorrect!"
0x102027  "Correct!"

Prompt referenced at: 0x10126d
Containing function: 0x10124d</code></pre>
                  </div>
                </div>
                <p>
                  The reference gives the agent a place to investigate, even
                  though the executable's original function names have been
                  removed.
                </p>
              </li>
              <li>
                <h4>Read the checker and its two helpers</h4>
                <div class="rea-query-pair">
                  <div class="code-block">
                    <div class="code-header"><span>Agent → REA</span></div>
                    <pre><code>analyze_function
{"procedure": "0x10124d"}

analyze_function
{"procedure": "0x101189"}

analyze_function
{"procedure": "0x101217"}</code></pre>
                  </div>
                  <div class="code-block">
                    <div class="code-header">
                      <span>REA → agent · selected instructions</span>
                    </div>
                    <pre><code>0x1012c1: CMP EDI, 0x24
0x1012c6: LEA RBX, [0x1040e0]
0x1012cd: LEA RBP, [0x104060]
0x1012d4: LEA R13, [RBX + 0x270]
0x1012e1: CALL 0x00101189
0x1012ec: CALL 0x00101217
0x1012f1: CMP dword ptr [RBP], EAX
0x1012f4: JNZ 0x00101335
0x1012f6: ADD RBX, 0x18</code></pre>
                  </div>
                </div>
                <p>
                  The first loop copies 36 character codes. The checking loop
                  decodes a mask, sums the selected codes and compares the
                  result with a stored number. Its <code>0x18</code>-byte steps
                  across <code>0x270</code> bytes give 26 masks.
                </p>
              </li>
            </ol>
            <p class="caption">
              These are selected results from a fresh REA analysis. The local
              target path is shortened for display; addresses refer to REA's
              imported image.
            </p>
          </section>

          <section class="article-section" id="mask">
            <h2>One check reveals one character</h2>
            <p>
              The checker arranges the input in a 6×6 grid. A mask chooses which
              cells contribute to a sum. Its compact encoding uses negative
              numbers to skip cells and positive numbers to select them.
            </p>
            <figure class="explanatory-figure ctf-mask-figure">
              <div
                class="figure-viewport"
                tabindex="0"
                role="region"
                aria-label="CTF mask equation; scroll horizontally on smaller screens"
              >
                <img
                  src="../../assets/figures/ctf-mask-equation.svg"
                  width="760"
                  height="475"
                  alt="The seventh mask skips 21 cells, selects position 21, then skips 14. Only that cell contributes to the sum. Its required character code is 55, which means the character is 7."
                  decoding="async"
                />
              </div>
              <figcaption>
                The seventh check selects just one position.
                <a href="../../assets/figures/ctf-mask-equation.svg"
                  >Open figure</a
                >.
              </figcaption>
            </figure>
            <h3 class="small-heading">
              Read the mask and its target from the binary
            </h3>
            <div class="rea-query-pair">
              <div class="code-block">
                <div class="code-header">
                  <span>Agent → REA · read_bytes</span>
                </div>
                <pre><code>{"address": "0x1040e0", "length": 624}
{"address": "0x104060", "length": 144}</code></pre>
              </div>
              <div class="code-block">
                <div class="code-header">
                  <span>REA → agent · seventh entries</span>
                </div>
                <pre><code>Mask at 0x104170:
eb 01 f2 00  →  -21, +1, -14, stop

Target at 0x104078:
37 00 00 00  →  55</code></pre>
              </div>
            </div>
            <p>
              The instruction <code>MOVSX</code> reads mask bytes as signed
              values. This is why <code>eb</code> means −21. The target is a
              little-endian integer. Together, these bytes tell the agent that
              <code>code[21] = 55</code>, so that character is <code>7</code>.
            </p>
          </section>

          <section class="article-section" id="code">
            <h2>From instructions to a readable check</h2>
            <p>
              Select a step to connect the summing helper and its caller to the
              same rule in C.
            </p>
            <div class="step-comparison" data-step-comparison>
              <div
                class="step-selector"
                role="group"
                aria-label="Follow the CTF check"
              >
                <button
                  type="button"
                  data-select-step="1"
                  aria-pressed="true"
                  aria-controls="ctf-assembly ctf-check ctf-step-detail"
                >
                  <span>01</span> Start
                </button>
                <button
                  type="button"
                  data-select-step="2"
                  aria-pressed="false"
                  aria-controls="ctf-assembly ctf-check ctf-step-detail"
                >
                  <span>02</span> Select
                </button>
                <button
                  type="button"
                  data-select-step="3"
                  aria-pressed="false"
                  aria-controls="ctf-assembly ctf-check ctf-step-detail"
                >
                  <span>03</span> Add
                </button>
                <button
                  type="button"
                  data-select-step="4"
                  aria-pressed="false"
                  aria-controls="ctf-assembly ctf-check ctf-step-detail"
                >
                  <span>04</span> Advance
                </button>
                <button
                  type="button"
                  data-select-step="5"
                  aria-pressed="false"
                  aria-controls="ctf-assembly ctf-check ctf-step-detail"
                >
                  <span>05</span> Compare
                </button>
              </div>
              <div class="code-comparison">
                <div class="code-block">
                  <div class="code-header">
                    <span>REA · selected original instructions</span
                    ><button
                      class="copy-button"
                      type="button"
                      data-copy="ctf-assembly"
                      aria-label="Copy CTF assembly"
                    >
                      Copy
                    </button>
                  </div>
                  <pre><code id="ctf-assembly"><span class="code-step is-active" data-step="1">0x10121c: MOV ECX, 0x0</span>

<span class="code-step" data-step="2">0x10122c: CMP dword ptr [RSI + RAX*0x1], 0x0
0x101230: JZ 0x00101223</span>

<span class="code-step" data-step="3">0x101232: ADD ECX, dword ptr [RDI + RAX*0x1]</span>

<span class="code-step" data-step="4">0x101223: ADD RAX, 0x4</span>

<span class="code-step" data-step="5">0x1012f1: CMP dword ptr [RBP], EAX
0x1012f4: JNZ 0x00101335</span></code></pre>
                </div>
                <div class="code-block">
                  <div class="code-header">
                    <span>Readable C · one-check summary</span
                    ><button
                      class="copy-button"
                      type="button"
                      data-copy="ctf-check"
                      aria-label="Copy readable CTF check"
                    >
                      Copy
                    </button>
                  </div>
                  <pre><code id="ctf-check">int check_one_mask(const int codes[36],
                   const int mask[36],
                   int target) {
<span class="code-step is-active" data-step="1">    int total = 0;</span>
<span class="code-step" data-step="4">    for (int i = 0; i &lt; 36; ++i) {</span>
<span class="code-step" data-step="2">        if (mask[i]) {</span>
<span class="code-step" data-step="3">            total += codes[i];</span>
        }
    }
<span class="code-step" data-step="5">    return total == target;</span>
}</code></pre>
                </div>
              </div>
              <div
                class="step-detail"
                id="ctf-step-detail"
                aria-live="polite"
                aria-atomic="true"
              >
                <p data-step-note="1">
                  <strong>01 · Start at zero.</strong> <code>ECX</code> holds
                  the running sum.
                </p>
                <p data-step-note="2" hidden>
                  <strong>02 · Check the mask cell.</strong> A zero value skips
                  the character; a nonzero value includes it.
                </p>
                <p data-step-note="3" hidden>
                  <strong>03 · Add a character code.</strong> The input's
                  integer at the same offset is added to the sum.
                </p>
                <p data-step-note="4" hidden>
                  <strong>04 · Move to the next cell.</strong> The original loop
                  advances four bytes per integer and visits six rows of six
                  cells.
                </p>
                <p data-step-note="5" hidden>
                  <strong>05 · Compare with the stored target.</strong> The
                  caller receives the sum in <code>EAX</code>. A mismatch jumps
                  to <code>Incorrect!</code>.
                </p>
              </div>
            </div>
            <p class="caption">
              The instructions come from the summing helper and its caller. The
              C is an explanatory summary with descriptive names and a flattened
              36-cell loop.
            </p>
          </section>

          <section class="article-section" id="solve">
            <h2>Solve the 26 equations</h2>
            <p>
              Most masks select several cells. For example, the first check adds
              16 character codes and requires a total of 1441. The overlapping
              selections give equations that a small Python script can solve
              together.
            </p>
            <div class="code-block">
              <div class="code-header">
                <span>Python · solver excerpt</span
                ><button
                  class="copy-button"
                  type="button"
                  data-copy="ctf-solver-excerpt"
                  aria-label="Copy CTF solver excerpt"
                >
                  Copy
                </button>
              </div>
              <pre><code id="ctf-solver-excerpt">from z3 import Int, Or, Solver, Sum, sat

codes = [Int(f"code_{i}") for i in range(36)]
solver = Solver()
alphabet = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789_{}"
for code in codes:
    solver.add(Or(*[code == ord(c) for c in alphabet]))
for code, char in zip(codes, "DUCTF{"):
    solver.add(code == ord(char))
solver.add(codes[-1] == ord("}"))

for selected, target in checks:
    solver.add(Sum([codes[i] for i in selected]) == target)

assert solver.check() == sat
model = solver.model()
print("".join(chr(model.eval(code).as_long()) for code in codes))</code></pre>
            </div>
            <p class="caption">
              Z3 is a solver that finds values satisfying these equations. This
              excerpt uses the extracted checks and assumes a
              <code>DUCTF{…}</code> flag with letters, digits, underscores and
              braces. The complete download includes all 26 masks and targets.
            </p>
            <a class="text-link" href="solve.py" download="solve.py"
              >Download the complete solver</a
            >
          </section>

          <section class="article-section" id="verify">
            <h2>Check the answer with the original program</h2>
            <p>
              REA's process capture records the original executable accepting
              the solved flag. Changing one selected character from
              <code>z</code> to <code>y</code> makes the first sum 1440 instead
              of 1441, and the program rejects it.
            </p>
            <div class="evidence-table-wrap">
              <table class="evidence-table">
                <thead>
                  <tr>
                    <th>Input</th>
                    <th>Observed output</th>
                    <th>Exit code</th>
                  </tr>
                </thead>
                <tbody>
                  <tr>
                    <td>Solver's flag</td>
                    <td><code>Correct!</code></td>
                    <td>0</td>
                  </tr>
                  <tr>
                    <td>One character changed</td>
                    <td><code>Incorrect!</code></td>
                    <td>255</td>
                  </tr>
                </tbody>
              </table>
            </div>
            <details class="evidence-details">
              <summary>Show the recovered flag and captured output</summary>
              <div class="code-block">
                <div class="code-header">
                  <span>REA · original program output</span
                  ><button
                    class="copy-button"
                    type="button"
                    data-copy="ctf-flag"
                    aria-label="Copy recovered flag"
                  >
                    Copy flag
                  </button>
                </div>
                <pre><code>What is the flag? <span id="ctf-flag">DUCTF{ezzzpzzz_07bcda7bfe81faf43caa}</span>
Correct!</code></pre>
              </div>
              <p>
                The recovered value also matches the flag in the organizers'
                published challenge metadata, checked after solving the binary.
              </p>
            </details>
            <details class="evidence-details">
              <summary>Source, target identity and analysis details</summary>
              <p>
                Fresh analysis and two process captures on 8 October 2026, using
                REA 4.1.0 with Ghidra 12.1.4 on Linux x64. The binary is a
                stripped x86-64 ELF, 15,248 bytes.
              </p>
              <div class="code-block">
                <div class="code-header">
                  <span>Original executable · SHA-256</span>
                </div>
                <pre><code>dcd3bec4f608e11f3a12ce461100aaf5f621851ee63a1f870d7c90d4e3dd51ae</code></pre>
              </div>
              <p>
                The string references, functions and constants were inspected
                before reading the organizers' source or solution. The Python
                solver and the diagram were built from those REA results.
              </p>
              <p>
```

`website/public/showcase/ctf/solve.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Solve the DownUnderCTF 2023 masked-squares handout from REA-extracted checks.

Requires Python 3 and z3-solver. The constants below were read from the original
ELF with SHA-256 dcd3bec4f608e11f3a12ce461100aaf5f621851ee63a1f870d7c90d4e3dd51ae.
Challenge by joseph / DownUnderCTF:
https://github.com/DownUnderCTF/Challenges_2023_Public/tree/b48f83db2984bc7fa2ec7879a32d7efb1be8d333/rev/masked-squares-flag-checker
"""

from z3 import Int, Or, Solver, Sum, sat

TARGETS = [1441, 2043, 1259, 2031, 1799, 746, 55, 1450, 1485, 1362, 611, 1314, 358, 1834, 1500, 1355, 2011, 1990, 1939, 1990, 278, 1859, 2111, 1510, 888, 1224]
RUNS = [
    (-5, 1, -2, 1, -1, 3, -3, 2, -1, 1, -1, 1, -1, 1, -1, 2, -3, 2, -2, 2),
    (-1, 1, -3, 2, -3, 2, -1, 1, -2, 3, -1, 1, -1, 7, -1, 3, -1, 2),
    (-1, 1, -1, 1, -1, 2, -1, 1, -6, 1, -1, 1, -2, 1, -1, 1, -1, 1, -4, 3, -1, 1, -2),
    (2, -1, 5, -3, 3, -1, 4, -1, 2, -1, 5, -3, 2, -3),
    (-1, 1, -3, 1, -1, 1, -2, 1, -1, 3, -1, 1, -1, 1, -2, 5, -1, 4, -1, 1, -3),
    (1, -2, 2, -8, 1, -7, 2, -1, 1, -3, 1, -2, 1, -4),
    (-21, 1, -14),
    (-2, 3, -4, 4, -5, 1, -2, 1, -1, 1, -2, 1, -2, 1, -1, 4, -1),
    (-4, 5, -3, 1, -5, 1, -3, 1, -2, 5, -4, 2),
    (-1, 2, -4, 1, -1, 4, -3, 1, -4, 1, -1, 2, -1, 1, -3, 1, -1, 2, -2),
    (-2, 1, -8, 1, -1, 1, -3, 1, -1, 1, -7, 1, -8),
    (1, -2, 5, -1, 1, -8, 3, -2, 1, -2, 1, -3, 1, -4, 1),
    (-3, 1, -9, 1, -2, 1, -17, 1, -1),
    (3, -5, 4, -1, 1, -2, 1, -1, 2, -3, 3, -1, 1, -1, 3, -1, 2, -1),
    (-2, 2, -3, 1, -1, 1, -1, 1, -1, 1, -7, 1, -1, 6, -1, 3, -1, 1, -1),
    (1, -5, 1, -2, 2, -1, 2, -1, 1, -1, 1, -5, 1, -1, 1, -1, 5, -4),
    (2, -3, 1, -5, 4, -2, 3, -2, 5, -1, 2, -1, 2, -1, 2),
    (-1, 1, -3, 1, -1, 2, -2, 1, -1, 7, -2, 3, -1, 4, -1, 1, -2, 1, -1),
    (2, -1, 1, -2, 2, -1, 2, -2, 5, -1, 1, -1, 2, -3, 2, -1, 1, -2, 2, -1, 1),
    (1, -3, 3, -1, 1, -2, 1, -1, 6, -1, 1, -1, 2, -2, 1, -1, 1, -1, 3, -1, 2),
    (-9, 1, -9, 1, -5, 1, -10),
    (1, -1, 2, -2, 1, -1, 9, -1, 1, -1, 1, -7, 2, -2, 1, -2, 1),
    (-1, 9, -1, 3, -1, 6, -1, 1, -1, 1, -2, 1, -3, 1, -4),
    (-2, 1, -3, 1, -1, 2, -5, 6, -1, 2, -2, 4, -1, 1, -4),
    (-2, 1, -4, 1, -1, 1, -2, 1, -3, 1, -3, 1, -3, 3, -6, 1, -2),
    (-8, 4, -2, 2, -1, 3, -5, 1, -2, 2, -1, 1, -4),
]


def decode_mask(runs):
    """Expand signed run lengths into 36 selected/unselected cells."""
    cells = [selected for run in runs for selected in [run > 0] * abs(run)]
    if len(cells) != 36:
        raise ValueError('A mask must cover all 36 input positions.')
    return [i for i, selected in enumerate(cells) if selected]


codes = [Int(f'code_{i}') for i in range(36)]
solver = Solver()
solver.set(timeout=60000)
# Analyst assumptions about a conventional flag's format and alphabet.
alphabet = 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789_{}'
for code in codes:
    solver.add(Or(*[code == ord(char) for char in alphabet]))
for code, char in zip(codes, 'DUCTF{'):
    solver.add(code == ord(char))
solver.add(codes[-1] == ord('}'))
for runs, target in zip(RUNS, TARGETS):
    solver.add(Sum([codes[i] for i in decode_mask(runs)]) == target)

status = solver.check()
if status != sat:
    raise SystemExit(f'No candidate returned: {status}. {solver.reason_unknown()}')
model = solver.model()
values = [model.eval(code).as_long() for code in codes]
if not all(sum(values[i] for i in decode_mask(runs)) == target
           for runs, target in zip(RUNS, TARGETS)):
    raise SystemExit('Candidate did not pass the extracted checks.')
print(''.join(map(chr, values)))
```

```html
            <h2>The project so far</h2>
            <p>
              The recovered code covers board and resource handling, brick hits,
              animations, particles and bonus production. Current builds provide
              inspection utilities and an analysis library. Work on the playable

          <section class="article-section" id="sound-pan">
            <h2>Finding the sound-pan calculation</h2>
            <p>
              When a brick is hit, its horizontal position is passed to the
              sound code. The investigation needed to recover how that screen
              coordinate becomes a left/right panning value.
            </p>
            <div class="agent-terminal">
              <div class="terminal-header">
                <span class="terminal-title"
                  ><span class="terminal-dots" aria-hidden="true"
                    ><i></i><i></i><i></i></span
                  >Your coding agent</span
                ><button
                  class="copy-button"
                  type="button"
                  data-copy="dxball-prompt"
                  aria-label="Copy example prompt"
                >
                  Copy
                </button>
              </div>
              <p class="terminal-prompt">
                <span class="prompt-symbol" aria-hidden="true">›</span
                ><span id="dxball-prompt"
                  >Use REA to find how DX-Ball calculates sound panning. Explain
                  the calculation and show the code.</span
                ><span class="terminal-cursor" aria-hidden="true"></span>
              </p>
            </div>
            <p class="caption">
              An example prompt for your coding agent, with the local executable
              available. The investigation below shows the REA queries and
              evidence behind the answer.
            </p>
            <p>
              The agent used REA to inspect the function, follow its brick-hit
              caller and read the constants from the executable. Those results
              supplied the input and arithmetic needed to write the C function
              below.
            </p>
            <p>
              The first function result for <code>0x406400</code> included
              pseudocode declaring <code>FUN_00406400(void)</code> and calling
              <code>__ftol()</code>. Its instruction view showed a stack input
              and floating-point operations. That discrepancy gave the agent a
              concrete reason to keep investigating.
            </p>
            <details class="evidence-details">
              <summary>The first decompiler view</summary>
              <div class="code-block">
                <div class="code-header">
                  <span>REA result · pseudocode excerpt</span>
                </div>
                <pre><code>longlong FUN_00406400(void)
{
  longlong lVar1;

  lVar1 = __ftol();
  return lVar1;
}</code></pre>
              </div>
              <p>
                The output shows a conversion call. Reading the instructions
                below reveals the input and the calculation feeding that call.
              </p>
            </details>

            <h3 class="small-heading">Three questions answered through REA</h3>
            <ol class="rea-queries">
              <li>
                <h4>Recover the missing input</h4>
                <div class="rea-query-pair">
                  <div class="code-block">
                    <div class="code-header">
                      <span>Agent → REA · <code>analyze_function</code></span>
                    </div>
                    <pre><code>{"procedure": "0x406400"}</code></pre>
                  </div>
                  <div class="code-block">
                    <div class="code-header">
                      <span>REA → agent · instruction excerpt</span>
                    </div>
                    <pre><code>0x406409: MOV EAX, dword ptr [EBP + 0x8]
0x40640c: MOV dword ptr [EBP + -0xc], EAX
0x40640f: FILD dword ptr [EBP + -0xc]</code></pre>
                  </div>
                </div>
                <p>
                  The function result includes instructions alongside pseudocode
                  and callers. Here, <code>[EBP+8]</code> exposes the integer
                  input missing from the decompiler view.
                </p>
              </li>
              <li>
                <h4>Follow the caller to understand the input</h4>
                <div class="rea-query-pair">
                  <div class="code-block">
                    <div class="code-header">
                      <span>Agent → REA · <code>analyze_function</code></span>
                    </div>
                    <pre><code>{"procedure": "0x411f40"}</code></pre>
                  </div>
                  <div class="code-block">
                    <div class="code-header">
                      <span>REA → agent · caller excerpt</span>
                    </div>
                    <pre><code>0x411f5b: ADD EAX, 0x14
0x411f5e: PUSH EAX
0x411f5f: CALL 0x00406400</code></pre>
                  </div>
                </div>
                <p>
                  REA identified this caller in the first result. Its preceding
                  instructions scale <code>tile_x</code> by 30; adding 20 gives
                  the brick's screen coordinate, <code>20 + 30 × tile_x</code>.
                </p>
              </li>
              <li>
                <h4>Read the values behind the memory addresses</h4>
                <div class="rea-query-pair">
                  <div class="code-block">
                    <div class="code-header">
                      <span
                        >Agent → REA · two
                        <code>read_bytes</code> requests</span
                      >
                    </div>
                    <pre><code>{"address": "0x420068", "length": 16}
{"address": "0x4210a0", "length": 8}</code></pre>
                  </div>
                  <div class="code-block">
                    <div class="code-header">
                      <span>REA byte results · decoded as doubles</span>
                    </div>
                    <pre><code>000000000000f93f → 1.5625
0000000000407f40 → 500.0
000000000000f03f → 1.0</code></pre>
                  </div>
                </div>
                <p>
                  The returned bytes establish the two arithmetic constants and
                  initial pan scale. The agent now has the values needed for the
                  C expression.
                </p>
              </li>
            </ol>

            <h3 class="small-heading">From REA's findings to C</h3>
            <p>
              Follow the five steps below. Each selection highlights the
              original instructions and the C lines they informed.
            </p>
            <div class="step-comparison" data-step-comparison>
              <div
                class="step-selector"
                role="group"
                aria-label="Follow the sound-pan calculation"
              >
                <button
                  type="button"
                  data-select-step="1"
                  aria-pressed="true"
                  aria-controls="pan-assembly pan-source pan-step-detail"
                >
                  <span>01</span> Input
                </button>
                <button
                  type="button"
                  data-select-step="2"
                  aria-pressed="false"
                  aria-controls="pan-assembly pan-source pan-step-detail"
                >
                  <span>02</span> Multiply
                </button>
                <button
                  type="button"
                  data-select-step="3"
                  aria-pressed="false"
                  aria-controls="pan-assembly pan-source pan-step-detail"
                >
                  <span>03</span> Subtract
                </button>
                <button
                  type="button"
                  data-select-step="4"
                  aria-pressed="false"
                  aria-controls="pan-assembly pan-source pan-step-detail"
                >
                  <span>04</span> Scale
                </button>
                <button
                  type="button"
                  data-select-step="5"
                  aria-pressed="false"
                  aria-controls="pan-assembly pan-source pan-step-detail"
                >
                  <span>05</span> Return
                </button>
              </div>
              <div class="code-comparison">
                <div class="code-block">
                  <div class="code-header">
                    <span>Original x86 · excerpt</span
                    ><button
                      class="copy-button"
                      type="button"
                      data-copy="pan-assembly"
                      aria-label="Copy original assembly excerpt"
                    >
                      Copy
                    </button>
                  </div>
                  <pre><code id="pan-assembly"><span class="code-step is-active" data-step="1">0x406409: MOV EAX, dword ptr [EBP + 0x8]
0x40640c: MOV dword ptr [EBP + -0xc], EAX
0x40640f: FILD dword ptr [EBP + -0xc]</span>
<span class="code-step" data-step="2">0x406415: FMUL double ptr [0x00420068]</span>
<span class="code-step" data-step="3">0x40641e: FSUB double ptr [0x00420070]</span>
<span class="code-step" data-step="4">0x406427: FMUL double ptr [0x004210a0]</span>
<span class="code-step" data-step="5">0x406430: CALL 0x0041678c
0x40643e: RET</span></code></pre>
                </div>
                <div class="code-block">
                  <div class="code-header">
                    <span>Reconstructed C</span
                    ><button
                      class="copy-button"
                      type="button"
                      data-copy="pan-source"
                      aria-label="Copy sound-pan function"
                    >
                      Copy
                    </button>
                  </div>
                  <pre><code id="pan-source">DxBallInt dxball_screen_pan(<span class="is-active" data-step="1">DxBallInt x</span>)
{
    double pan;
<span class="code-step is-active" data-step="1">    pan = (double)x;</span>
<span class="code-step" data-step="2">    pan = pan * 1.5625;</span>
<span class="code-step" data-step="3">    pan = pan - 500.0;</span>
<span class="code-step" data-step="4">    pan = pan * dxball_pan_scale;</span>
<span class="code-step" data-step="5">    return (DxBallInt)pan;</span>
}</code></pre>
                </div>
              </div>
              <div
                class="step-detail"
                id="pan-step-detail"
                aria-live="polite"
                aria-atomic="true"
              >
                <p data-step-note="1">
                  <strong>01 · Read the input.</strong>
                  The instruction view in REA's function result reads
                  <code>[EBP+8]</code> and uses <code>FILD</code> to load the
                  integer. Following its caller through REA establishes the
                  screen-coordinate meaning of the C parameter <code>x</code>.
                </p>
                <p data-step-note="2" hidden>
                  <strong>02 · Multiply by 1.5625.</strong>
                  <code>FMUL</code> reads the double at <code>0x420068</code>.
                  The bytes returned by REA's <code>read_bytes</code> decode to
                  <code>1.5625</code>; the C uses the same constant.
                </p>
                <p data-step-note="3" hidden>
                  <strong>03 · Subtract 500.0.</strong> <code>FSUB</code> reads
                  the double at <code>0x420070</code>. REA's byte result decodes
                  to <code>500.0</code>, shifting the calculation's center to
                  screen coordinate <code>320</code>.
                </p>
                <p data-step-note="4" hidden>
                  <strong>04 · Apply the stored scale.</strong> The second
                  <code>FMUL</code> reads <code>0x4210a0</code>. That global is
                  named <code>dxball_pan_scale</code> in the maintained source.
                  REA's second byte read establishes its initial value of
                  <code>1.0</code>.
                </p>
                <p data-step-note="5" hidden>
                  <strong>05 · Return an integer.</strong> The call at
                  <code>0x406430</code> reaches <code>__ftol</code>, identified
                  in REA's callee results. The C casts the result to
                  <code>DxBallInt</code>; original-x86 comparisons check the
                  returned value.
                </p>
              </div>
            </div>
            <p class="caption">
              The assembly excerpt selects the input, arithmetic and return
              instructions. The full listing below also includes the intervening
              stores and function setup and cleanup.
            </p>
            <details class="evidence-details">
              <summary>Full assembly and supporting evidence</summary>
              <div class="code-block">
                <div class="code-header">
                  <span>REA result · 0x406400–0x40643e</span
                  ><button
                    class="copy-button"
                    type="button"
                    data-copy="pan-assembly-full"
                    aria-label="Copy complete sound-pan assembly"
                  >
                    Copy
                  </button>
                </div>
                <pre><code id="pan-assembly-full">0x406400: PUSH EBP
0x406401: MOV EBP, ESP
0x406403: SUB ESP, 0xc
0x406406: PUSH EBX
0x406407: PUSH ESI
0x406408: PUSH EDI
0x406409: MOV EAX, dword ptr [EBP + 0x8]
0x40640c: MOV dword ptr [EBP + -0xc], EAX
0x40640f: FILD dword ptr [EBP + -0xc]
0x406412: FST double ptr [EBP + -0x8]
0x406415: FMUL double ptr [0x00420068]
0x40641b: FST double ptr [EBP + -0x8]
0x40641e: FSUB double ptr [0x00420070]
0x406424: FST double ptr [EBP + -0x8]
0x406427: FMUL double ptr [0x004210a0]
0x40642d: FST double ptr [EBP + -0x8]
0x406430: CALL 0x0041678c
0x406435: JMP 0x0040643a
0x40643a: POP EDI
0x40643b: POP ESI
0x40643c: POP EBX
0x40643d: LEAVE
0x40643e: RET</code></pre>
              </div>
              <h3>What the caller supplies</h3>
              <p>
                The brick-hit function at <code>0x411f40</code> scales its tile
                coordinate by 30, adds 20, then pushes it before the call:
              </p>
              <div class="code-block">
                <pre><code>0x411f50: MOV EAX, dword ptr [EBP + 0x8]
0x411f53: ADD EAX, EAX
0x411f55: LEA EAX, [EAX + EAX*0x2]
0x411f58: LEA EAX, [EAX + EAX*0x4]
0x411f5b: ADD EAX, 0x14
0x411f5e: PUSH EAX
0x411f5f: CALL 0x00406400
0x411f64: ADD ESP, 0x4</code></pre>
              </div>
              <h3>What the data reads establish</h3>
              <div class="evidence-table-wrap">
                <table class="evidence-table">
                  <caption>
                    REA byte reads, decoded as little-endian doubles
                  </caption>
                  <thead>
                    <tr>
                      <th scope="col">Address</th>
                      <th scope="col">Value</th>
                      <th scope="col">Used for</th>
                    </tr>
                  </thead>
                  <tbody>
                    <tr>
                      <td><code>0x420068</code></td>
                      <td><code>1.5625</code></td>
                      <td>First multiplication</td>
                    </tr>
                    <tr>
                      <td><code>0x420070</code></td>
                      <td><code>500.0</code></td>
                      <td>Subtraction</td>
                    </tr>
                    <tr>
                      <td><code>0x4210a0</code></td>
                      <td><code>1.0</code> initially</td>
                      <td>Stored pan scale</td>
                    </tr>
                  </tbody>
                </table>
              </div>
              <p class="caption">
                Recorded with REA 4.1.0 for the hash-pinned DX-Ball 1.07 target.
                The linked investigation notes retain the Evidence IDs.
              </p>
            </details>
            <p class="caption">
              <a
                href="https://github.com/N0zoM1z0/dx-ball/blob/a55dca27ec0a07018c1b2c95ae2be027f7d8c3c4/src/gameplay.c#L41"
                >Maintained source</a
              >
              ·
              <a
                href="https://github.com/N0zoM1z0/dx-ball/blob/a55dca27ec0a07018c1b2c95ae2be027f7d8c3c4/docs/GAMEPLAY_OWNER.md"
                >Investigation notes and evidence references</a
              >
            </p>
          </section>

          <section class="article-section" id="checking">
            <h2>Checking the recovered function</h2>
            <p>
              The recovered function passes two checks: its return values match
              the original, and its compiled bytes match the executable.
            </p>
            <div class="verification">
              <div>
                <h3>3,205 behavior cases</h3>
                <p>
                  The tests execute the original x86 function and compare its
                  return value with the maintained C. They cover every integer
                  position from 0 to 640 at five pan scales: 0, 0.5, 1, 20 and
                  −1.
                </p>
              </div>
              <div>
                <h3>63 matching bytes</h3>
                <p>
                  The C function is compiled with the pinned VC4.0 toolchain.
                  Compiler replay matches the complete function after applying
                  the reviewed relocations and checking the referenced
                  constants.
                </p>
              </div>
            </div>
            <p class="small-heading">
              At a scale of 1, the recovered calculation returns −500 at the
              left edge, 0 at the center and 500 at the right edge. The next
              part of the audio work is integrating that value with the game's
              sound backend.
            </p>
            <p>
              <a
                href="https://github.com/N0zoM1z0/dx-ball/blob/a55dca27ec0a07018c1b2c95ae2be027f7d8c3c4/docs/BUILD_MATCHING.md"
                >Read the compiler replay details</a
              >
            </p>
          </section>

          <section class="article-section" id="continue">
            <h2>Continue the investigation</h2>
            <p>
              The same approach is being used for particle updates, explosion
              queues and bonus generation: inspect the relevant functions,
              recover their state and dependencies, then compare the
              implementation with the original.
            </p>
            <p>
              To inspect the sound-pan function yourself, follow the DX-Ball
              project's setup instructions and supply its matching original
              target. Then run:
            </p>
            <div class="code-block">
              <div class="code-header">
                <span>In the DX-Ball checkout</span
                ><button
                  class="copy-button"
                  type="button"
                  data-copy="pan-command"
                  aria-label="Copy DX-Ball analysis command"
                >
                  Copy
                </button>
              </div>
              <pre><code id="pan-command">scripts/rea function original/DXBALL.EXE 0x00406400 \
  --snapshot .analysis/rea/dxball.snapshot.json --json</code></pre>
            </div>
            <ul class="reading-list">
              <li>
                <a href="https://github.com/N0zoM1z0/dx-ball"
                  >DX-Ball repository</a
                ><span>Current source, progress and local setup.</span>
              </li>
              <li>
                <a href="../../guides/native/">REA analysis workflow</a
                ><span
                  >Follow the calculation, then use the same approach with your
                  own binary.</span
                >
              </li>
              <li>
                <a
                  href="https://github.com/N0zoM1z0/dx-ball/blob/a55dca27ec0a07018c1b2c95ae2be027f7d8c3c4/docs/ENTITIES_OWNER.md"
                  >Particles and bonus production</a
                ><span
                  >A larger investigation into state, queues and pixel
                  writes.</span
                >
              </li>
            </ul>
            <div class="actions">
              <a class="button" href="../../get-started/"
                >Start with your own target</a
              >
            </div>
          </section>
```

```html
        <h1>How Notion copies<br />text and HTML.</h1>
        <p class="lede">
          Trace a clipboard call from Notion's page API, through the preload and
          main process, to Electron's clipboard writer.
        </p>
        <p class="page-meta">Notion Desktop 7.6.1 · JavaScript · REA</p>

            <span class="flow-label">01 · Page-facing API</span>
            <span class="flow-node"><code>clipboard.write(data)</code></span>
            <span class="flow-note"
              >The preload exposes a callable method.</span
            >
          </li>
          <li>
            <span class="flow-label">02 · Preload wrapper</span>
            <span class="flow-node"><code>ipcRenderer.invoke</code></span>
            <span class="flow-note"
              >The wrapper sends the channel and arguments.</span
            >
          </li>
          <li>
            <span class="flow-label">03 · Main-process handler</span>
            <span class="flow-node"><code>ipcMain.handle</code></span>
            <span class="flow-note"
              >The receiver checks which page sent it.</span
            >
          </li>
          <li>
            <span class="flow-label">04 · System clipboard</span>
            <span class="flow-node"><code>clipboard.write(data)</code></span>
            <span class="flow-note"
              >Electron writes the supplied text and HTML.</span
            >
          </li>
```
